543527|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 equity AUM rose 1.7% QoQ to INR1.37 lakh crore despite INR1,867 crore MTM drag, with record INR4,137 crore net sales.
543527|2026-09.overview: Quarterly average AUM reached INR1.43 lakh crore, up 8% QoQ and 21% YoY, while revenue from operations rose 11.8% QoQ and operating profit rose 15.4% QoQ with margin expanding 80 bps to 26.4%. Reported PAT fell 4.1% QoQ to INR71.7 crore because other income dropped about 82% to INR3.8 crore on bond-yield and hybrid-portfolio mark-to-market reversals. Management said the sharp market correction in late October leaves current AUM slightly below the first-half average of INR1.38 lakh crore. The bulk of the call went to a proposed insurance distribution regulation (IDA vs IDE commission gap), where management said insurance is about 12% of PBT and the impact is uncertain.

segments.name: Mutual fund distribution
segments.commentary: Quarterly average AUM up 8% QoQ; MF yield stable at 88-89 bps. Equity AUM share ex-ETF rose from 2.59% to 2.7% YoY; SIP market share rose from 3.49% to 3.73%.

segments.name: Insurance distribution
segments.commentary: Insurance revenue up 35% QoQ; general insurance fresh premium up 54% QoQ and 62% YoY; life fresh premium up 37% QoQ and 45% YoY. Management puts the insurance contribution at about 12% of profit (PBT).

segments.name: Other financial and non-financial products (incl. PMS)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 14% QoQ, led by PMS distribution; average PMS AUM grew 37% YoY to about INR2,020 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management expects MF PMS framework to be operational from April 2027; company is applying for MF PMS license via subsidiary renamed Prudent Asset Management Private Limited (formerly Prutech).

Management said that if the insurance proposal were implemented as drafted (IDE renewal commission 5% vs 10% for IDA), it would hurt the insurance business, but called that scenario unlikely; the final regulation is awaited before giving numbers.
Management expects renewal commission cuts to be passed on to POSPs from April onwards, reducing absolute margin on that book.
Company is awaiting SEBI's final FICP framework before launching online bond distribution through its OBPP license.
capex_capacity: Pan-India branch network and tech platform; around 700 sales employees cited as capacity to support distributors moving into MF.
SIF certification: 1,792 distributors certified; SIF AUM nearly INR900 crore.
Onboarded about 3,541 new distributors in H1 FY27, nearly 30% higher than H1 FY26.
demand_pricing: Industry net sales were weak; Prudent's net sales were the highest ever. Management says redemptions are lower than before and SIP cancellations rose.
SIP contributes about 50% of Prudent's gross sales; management said its market-share gains partly reflect this SIP mix in a weak fresh-flow market.

Management said competition from platforms, banks and national distributors is rising, but it is holding market share; it said some large players are moderating payouts after 2-3 years of higher payouts.
Management said MF PMS fee cap of 1% is close to current ~80-90 bps realisation on MF, so margin should be similar.
Commissions as a share of non-insurance operating revenue rose to 62.6% from 61.4% in Q1, which management attributed mainly to a INR2.5 crore additional trail provision (INR1.75 crore booked in Q2).

qa_highlights.question: How would a level playing field between IDEs and IDAs change the economics, and where are insurance margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said insurance margins are broadly in line with mutual funds; it will size the opportunity once the final regulation is out, but IDEs need at least parity with IDAs to remain viable.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 12% insurance profit contribution at risk, and will POSPs survive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the entire 12% will not disappear overnight; renewal books may persist, and the impact will be gradual. It gave no firm guidance on the eventual impact.

qa_highlights.question: Will competition for distributors pressure MF payouts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new entrants with higher payouts cannot sustain them long-term and that payouts are moderating; it does not see a margin challenge from new entrants.

qa_highlights.question: Why did MF yield rise slightly this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin is static at about 88.8 bps; the uptick reflected one additional revenue day, not mix.

qa_highlights.question: What share of POSPs overlap with MFDs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said more than 90% overlap at family level between MF distributors and POSPs.

qa_highlights.question: Will PMS MF cannibalise MFD business and what realisation is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PMS MF should attract new distributors, with fee capped at 1%, close to current 80-90 bps earnings, so margin should be similar to MF.

qa_highlights.question: Why did market share gains occur and how much is in small and mid cap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed gains to higher net sales, lower redemptions and a SIP-heavy book, noting SIPs are concentrated in small and mid cap; it warned share gains may stall if fresh gross flows recover.

risks_watch: Proposed insurance distribution regulation (IDA 10% vs IDE 5% renewal commission in health): insurance is about 12% of PBT; final rules pending.
Other income is volatile (INR3.8 crore in Q2 vs INR20.8 crore in Q1) due to bond yields and hybrid MTM.
Market correction in late October 2026 means current AUM is slightly below the H1 average; watch SIP cancellations and fresh flows.
Commissions as a share of non-insurance operating revenue rose to 62.6% from 61.4% QoQ; watch payout trends.
Timing and licensing for MF PMS (April 2027) and FICP framework for online bonds.
Market share gains are partly tied to SIP mix and may not persist if fresh gross flows recover.
543527|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on operating performance and market share, but guarded on the insurance regulation, where management repeatedly declined to give quantified guidance. Several answers relied on historical analogies and qualitative reassurance. Some answers were disrupted by line drops, leaving parts of the Q&A incomplete.
key_quotes: This is the highest quarterly net sales in our history.
So IDE earn almost 50% less than the agent for exactly the same business.
I don't think entire 12% will disappear overnight.
So practically, you can say that more than 90% overlap is there between mutual fund and the POSP.

financial_highlights.change: Highest quarterly net sales in company history
Helped by one additional revenue day; MF yield 88-89 bps
+37.6% YoY; operating margin 26.1% vs 22.7% last year

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Operating margin rose 80 bps QoQ to 26.4% and H1 margin is 26.1% vs 22.7% last year, but renewal commission pass-through to POSPs from April and rising commissions (62.6% of non-insurance revenue vs 61.4% in Q1) cap upside.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Pan-India branch network and about 700 sales staff support distributor onboarding (3,541 new distributors in H1, up ~30% YoY), and the MF PMS framework starts April 2027, but no new physical capacity or dated build-out was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Record INR4,137 crore quarterly net sales, SIP market share up to 3.73% from 3.49%, and SIP book up 17.2% YoY to INR1,272 crore, though AUM is slightly below H1 average after the late-October correction and share gains may stall if gross flows recover.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed and no utilisation figure was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No forward revenue or margin guidance was given, and management stated the 88.8 bps MF yield is sustainable rather than rising.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: A proposed insurance commission cut (IDE renewal at 5% vs 10% for IDA) affects about 12% of PBT; management called the drafted scenario unlikely but gave no quantified impact while the final rule is awaited.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: MF PMS framework is due from April 2027 with a company licence application under way via Prudent Asset Management, and online bond distribution awaits SEBI's FICP framework, with no date given.

rows.label: Insurance distribution regulation (IDA vs IDE commission gap)
rows.why: Insurance is about 12% of PBT and the drafted IDE renewal commission of 5% vs 10% for IDA would hurt the business, but management called that scenario unlikely and the final rule is awaited.

rows.label: MF PMS launch via Prudent Asset Management
rows.why: Management expects the MF PMS framework from April 2027 and the company is applying for the licence; the 1% fee cap is close to the current 80-90 bps MF realisation, so margin should be similar.

rows.label: Other income volatility
rows.why: Other income fell to INR3.8 crore from INR20.8 crore in Q1 on bond-yield and hybrid MTM, so reported PAT can swing even as operating profit grows.

tone.note: Management was confident on record net sales, share gains and operating margin, but guarded on the insurance regulation and gave no quantified impact; analysts pressed on insurance economics and POSP survival, and some Q&A answers were cut off by line drops.

543528|2026-03.headline: Venus Pipes Q4 FY26 revenue rose 17% YoY to INR302.2 crores, with EBITDA margin at 16.3% and PAT up 7% to INR25.4 crores.
543528|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 17% YoY to INR302.2 crores and FY26 revenue grew 22% to INR1,166.8 crores. Export sales fell to INR87.8 crores from INR112.5 crores on Middle East disruption, while domestic demand stayed robust. The company completed its seamless and welded capex program and announced a spooling foray for data centers backed by a INR185 crores LOI. Management guided to more than 20% growth in FY27 and EBITDA margin above FY26's 16.3%, rising to 18% by FY28.

financial_highlights.change: +19% YoY vs INR41.6 crores; margin vs 16.1% in Q4 FY25
down from INR112.5 crores in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Seamless pipes
segments.commentary: 59% of Q4 FY26 revenue, growing 18% YoY; FY26 volume growth above 15%. Seamless utilisation was 90-95% for FY26 and similar in Q4.

segments.name: Welded pipes
segments.commentary: 34% of Q4 FY26 revenue, growing 15% YoY; FY26 volume growth around 10%. Utilisation was around 60-65% for FY26 and similar in Q4.

segments.name: Others / fittings / spooling
segments.commentary: 7% of Q4 FY26 revenue. Fittings capacity commenced operations on 3 June 2026; spooling facility (capex around INR70 crores) targeted for commercial production by mid Q3 FY27 and full operation by December 2026.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 exports INR87.8 crores, down from INR112.5 crores YoY, but still above 30% of revenue. FY26 exports grew 18%; current order book is about 40% export.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at more than 20%, including pipes, fittings and spooling; management says this is kept within current geopolitical assumptions.
EBITDA margin in FY27 to be higher than FY26's 16.3%, moving to about 17% and then 18% blended by FY28; management says the intent is to improve every quarter.
FY27 consolidated capex guided at INR90-100 crores.
Export share guided at 30-35% going forward.
Spooling business targeted at about 3x asset turn, with EBITDA margins above the current base business; management did not confirm a 35% margin benchmark cited by an analyst.
Working capital guided at about 120 days of sales, with no major change expected for new data-center business.
capex_capacity: Capex program fully commissioned: installed capacity 27,600 MTPA welded pipes and 20,400 MTPA seamless pipes, plus fittings capacity.

Seamless expansion raised from 4,800 to 6,000 MTPA: 1,800 MTPA operational November 2025 and 4,200 MTPA operational on the day of the call (26 May 2026). Company is now 100% backward integrated for mother hollow on the 20,400 MTPA seamless capacity.
Total capex on seamless, welded and fittings for the expansion is more than INR200 crores; at full utilisation, asset turn is at least around 3x.
Spooling and fabrication facility with fittings machinery, capex around INR70 crores; trial runs by end Q2 FY27 and commercial production by mid Q3 FY27.
Tandem JCO press installed for longer welded pipes (INR12 crores); management says capacity is largely unchanged and the gain is in SKU range and tender eligibility.
Acquired 15 acres of adjacent land for future expansion.
demand_pricing: Order book INR450 crores excluding a INR185 crores data-center LOI, which management says is from a single data-center customer and is executable in about 15 months.
Separately, the company is L1 on BHEL tenders worth about INR50 crores, expected to be awarded in 30-45 days; less than 60% of the existing BHEL order had been executed by Q4.
Management cited about INR685 crores of total visibility (order book, LOI and BHEL L1), about 30% export, giving visibility for the next 2-3 quarters.
Domestic demand cited from CNG, power, oil and gas, engineering and chemicals; new approvals reported from oil and gas in the US and Middle East.
Middle East orders are currently weak; management expects recovery if the conflict eases.
Pricing rose 5-7% in FY26, partly grade mix; management expects RM cost increases to flow through and says a prolonged period of high RM prices may weigh on margins.
EBITDA per tonne in FY26 about INR65 per kg (totality basis; blended figure not given).

qa_highlights.question: When will the spooling business start, what revenue and margin does it carry, and how long will the INR185 crores order take?
qa_highlights.answer: Target start by end of calendar 2026 with about 3x asset turn and higher margin than the base business; the order is executable in about 15 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth of at least 20%, and EBITDA margin above FY26's 16.3%, moving to 17% and then 18% by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the PAT stay flat at INR25-26 crores over about nine quarters despite the investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PAT growth should follow as most capex is complete, with the value-added projects expected to lift PAT in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% FY27 growth guidance at risk given a lower order book (INR450 crores vs about INR575 crores a year ago) and softer exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the BHEL L1 orders, the data-center LOI, new fittings, and the expanded seamless capacity to 6,000 MTPA; it said FY26 was harder yet grew 22%.

qa_highlights.question: How does the spooling business differ from Ratnamani's, and could it enter nuclear spooling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Ratnamani focuses on nuclear spooling, while Venus targets data-center spooling. Nuclear entry has limitations but is a possible long-term goal. It declined to give a margin estimate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the BHEL order flow?
qa_highlights.answer: BHEL tenders are expected to open from August to September, with more orders in Q2 FY27, and BHEL is working to expedite delayed orders.

risks_watch: Export softness from the Middle East conflict; Q4 exports fell about 22% YoY and management says Middle East order flow has not yet recovered.
Raw material and gas cost inflation; management warned that prolonged high RM prices may affect margins.
Spooling execution: trial runs, commercial start timing (mid Q3 FY27), and the dependence on a single LOI customer.
Order book fell to INR450 crores (vs about INR575 crores a year earlier); the 20% FY27 growth guidance depends on new orders and BHEL tenders.
Welded pipe utilisation of only 60-65% for FY26, despite the welded capacity being unchanged.
Cash conversion: EBITDA to CFO was 59% in FY26; PAT has been flat at about INR25-26 crores for about nine quarters.
543528|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth and the data-center opportunity, but cautious on exports and raw material costs. Management was often vague on spooling unit economics, utilisation per tonne and margins, deferring to one-on-one calls.
key_quotes: I am proud to share that entire capex program has now been fully commissioned.
So, at least for next 2 to 3 quarters, we have the good visibility from Europe market, US market as well as from domestic market.
It is like PEB for piping, you can say.

543528|2026-06.headline: Venus Pipes Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16% to INR320.5 crore and EBITDA hit a record INR51.5 crore, with margin flat at 16.1%.
543528|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR320.5 crore, up 16% YoY, with management calling it the highest-ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA. EBITDA rose 14.7% to INR51.5 crore, but margin of 16.1% was broadly flat versus 16.2%, and PAT grew 6.5% to INR26.4 crore. Domestic revenue grew 31% to INR227 crore, while exports fell to INR94 crore from INR103 crore on geopolitical disruption. Fittings, value-added seamless and welded capacity started in May 2026, and the data-centre spooling line (about INR70 crore capex, INR185 crore LOI) is targeted for end-2026 commissioning.

vs 16.2% in Q1 FY26, broadly flat

financial_highlights.change: vs ~INR450 crore last quarter per analyst

segments.name: Welded pipes & tubes
segments.commentary: Revenue 39% of mix, up 21% YoY; utilisation around 60%, with value-added tubing started in FY26.

segments.name: Fittings
segments.commentary: Commercial production started May 2026; management expects 5-7% of FY27 revenue and 8-10% in FY28, though approvals are still in progress.

Management said revenue could double by around FY29-FY30, with a verbal reference to INR2,500 crore before that point; this was not formally guided.
capex_capacity: Seamless capacity added at the end of May 2026; utilisation expected to rise each quarter, with a target of more than 80-85% for seamless and more than 60-65% for welded in FY27-28.

Spooling facility (about INR70 crore capex) targeted to start end of Q3 FY27, with major portion of data-centre capex targeted before December 2026.
Management said spooling output should be at least 3x asset turn in revenue.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand healthy across oil & gas, chemical, pharma, engineering and power; order inflow mix includes repeat power customers and new engineering/chemical customers.
Export order inflow strong from the US; export revenue dipped on geopolitical disruption, with Q2 pickup intended but container and geopolitical issues flagged.
Realisations rose with steel prices, and EBITDA per kg improved.
Management said competition exists but is not undercutting in pipes; new entrants in spooling were noted.

qa_highlights.question: What are utilisation levels and is the ~20% growth guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Welded utilisation about 60%, seamless about 85-90%; FY27 growth guidance maintained at a similar level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did order book rise about INR150 crore in a quarter, and from which sectors?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly power, engineering, chemical and oil & gas; the order book stood above INR600 crore, plus the INR185 crore spooling LOI.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 margin outlook and FY28 target?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 margin below 17%; target about 18% over the next two years, with fittings and spooling contributing from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt about INR325 crore at June 30, 2026; FY27 capex about INR100 crore, of which INR70 crore spooling.

qa_highlights.question: Why did data-centre revenue expectations move up versus the earlier spooling timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects part of the capex to overlap Q4 FY27, with the major portion done before December 2026 and execution through December 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the EU safeguard quota not the cause of the export decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to geopolitical factors; the EU quota was cut 25%, and India has historically exceeded the quota.

risks_watch: Export decline (INR94 crore vs INR103 crore) from geopolitical and container disruption; the Q2 recovery is uncertain.
Fittings approvals and spooling customer qualification may take months, so the ramp-up timeline is uncertain.

Inconsistency on the spooling revenue timeline: INR37 crore run-rate vs ~INR70 crore FY27 target versus Q4 commissioning.

543529|2026-03.headline: Delhivery FY26 revenue reached ~10,486 crore with 7.3% service EBITDA and first full-year FCF positive at ~89 crore, a year ahead of plan.
543529|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was about 2,848 crore with PAT of about 87 crore (~3% margin) and adjusted EBITDA of 151 crore. FY26 was the first year of the Ecom Express integration, with over a billion express packages and about 2 million MT of PTL freight. Supply chain services (SCS) reached breakeven on adjusted EBITDA after a service EBITDA turnaround to 10.9%. Management said the company turned FCF positive, one year ahead of plan, despite integration costs; cash stood above 4,500 crore.

segments.name: Express

543539|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose about 84% to INR189 crore and PAT 26% to INR29.14 crore, but margins compressed on construction-cost inflation and new-project start-up costs.
543539|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 revenue of about INR189 crore (up ~84% from INR102 crore) and EBITDA of INR38.46 crore (up 35%), with PAT of INR29.14 crore (up 26%). Margins moderated on project mix, war-related construction input inflation, and early-stage costs on newly started projects. Two projects (Rashmi Vasudev and Rashmi Celestia) received OC and were handed over during the year, and the company remains debt-free. Management guided that margins will return to prior levels in FY27 and that Rashmi Square and Rashmi Signature are the key cash-generating projects.

No dividend under consideration; board focused on project execution.

Six ongoing projects after Rashmi Icon and Rashmi Avenu were started in FY26.

Company stated it is asset-light and funds internal project cash flows from high-margin Rashmi Square and Rashmi Signature; no structured debt planned for Icon or Avenu.
demand_pricing: Management reports healthy demand in Borivali, Kandivali and Dahisar with no slowdown; buyers returning from abroad and NRIs buying in India are cited as drivers.
Q3 seasonality (Shraadh period Dec to mid-Jan) cited as a slow period; management expects Q1 FY27 bookings to reflect better footfall and conversion.
Raw material cost inflation affecting only Rashmi Square and Rashmi Signature, where materials are being procured at higher prices; management said impact is limited.

qa_highlights.question: How much raw material inflation hit the company and was it passed through to realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only Rashmi Square and Rashmi Signature were hit minorly; other projects are unaffected and the overall impact is limited at the current execution stage.

qa_highlights.question: What is the blended realisation and will it rise?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 realisation was about INR25,000 to 27,000 per sq ft; management said it will not fall and Rashmi Square is targeted at INR27,000 to 28,000.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins decline and when will they normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited construction cost inflation from the war and early-stage costs of two new projects, expecting margins to return to prior levels in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a need for structured debt for Icon or Avenu?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no; funding will come from internal cash flows of Rashmi Square and Rashmi Signature, and borrowings are minimal.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend policy and capital employed?
qa_highlights.answer: No dividend under consideration for now as the board prioritises projects; capital employed estimated at INR80 to 90 crore as on 31 March.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin recovery to prior levels in FY27 is management's expectation; FY26 margins fell and the cost drivers (war-related input inflation) remain open.
Rashmi Manorath has weak sales traction; company is shifting to channel partners and internal sales policies.
Rashmi Signature booking conversion (about 50% per management, analyst cited 57% of carpet area) needs to rise to the targeted ~75%.
Q4 FY26 revenue growth (analyst cited 158% YoY) and Q1 FY27 bookings are key checkpoints.

rows.why: Margins fell in FY26 (EBITDA up 35% to INR38.46 crore on revenue up ~84% to INR189 crore, so margin compressed) and war-related input inflation on Rashmi Square and Rashmi Signature remains open; Rashmi Manorath has weak traction and Rashmi Signature is at ~50% booked vs a ~75% target.

543539|2026-06.headline: Modis Navnirman Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27.92% YoY to INR58.26 crore; PAT up 25.81% to INR8.54 crore, though EBITDA margin fell to about 20%.
543539|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 27.92% YoY to INR58.26 crore and 13.15% QoQ, with EBITDA up 14.25% YoY to INR11.65 crore and PAT up 25.81% YoY to INR8.54 crore. Management attributed the margin squeeze to war-related material and labour cost spikes in April-May, which it said have since stabilised. The company added Khar (Rashmi Icon/redevelopment) to its Mumbai footprint, bringing the portfolio to 25 projects (six ongoing, 14 completed, five upcoming). Management gave no quantified FY27 project-addition target, only that two to three projects are likely in FY27.

segments.name: Mumbai redevelopment projects
segments.commentary: Six ongoing, 14 completed, five upcoming; 25 projects in total across Malad, Kandivali, Borivali, Dahisar, Goregaon, Khar. Revenue recognised on percentage-of-completion (Ind AS 115).

segments.name: Rashmi Square / Rashmi Signature
segments.commentary: Together about 60% of Q1 revenue per analyst's question, which management did not dispute. Square at 22 slabs and roughly 80% of inventory booked; Signature at 20th slab and roughly 50-70% booked (figures varied within the call).

guidance_outlook: Management expects two to three new redevelopment projects in FY27, with no guarantee given tender uncertainty.

Four pipeline projects with aggregate GDV above INR800 crore: Rashmi Paradise to start in Q1 FY27 (this quarter), Rashmi Gold and Shectal in Q3, Khar in Q4; Govind Dalvi on hold due to a government stay on a 500-metre area.
Management cited healthy margins of around 20-30% expected per project, and 19-20% margins on upcoming projects.
Square and Signature margins are slightly below underwriting due to war-time material purchases, but not expected to be majorly hit over a two to two-and-a-half year timeline.
Management has not yet set a leverage ceiling or capital-employed framework per project.
capex_capacity: Under construction: about 12.11 lakh sq ft; upcoming pipeline about 10.5 lakh sq ft (per analyst's question, not disputed).
Rashmi Square completed 22 slabs; Rashmi Signature 20th slab; Rashmi Delight 14th slab; Rashmi Manorath 13th slab; Rashmi Icon and Rashmi Avenue at plinth stage.
Rashmi Signature and Square expected to be handed over with occupancy certificate in Q3 FY27.
Asset-light redevelopment model: partners with societies rather than buying open-market land.
demand_pricing: Management said pricing trends are similar to before, with no significant volatility; pricing is micro-market and project specific.
Management views Mumbai demand as stable with no decline expected over the next few years, though supply has risen due to government moves on MHADA and SRA land.
Demand exists for both luxury and affordable segments; product positioning varies by micro-market (larger homes in Kandivali/Borivali).
Labour availability and cost were described as not an issue at any project now, after war-time shortages in April-May.
Expansion limited to Bombay; Parle in tender, Ghatkopar under discussion, nothing finalised. Other Indian cities open in principle.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from about 22.3% to about 19.8% despite 28% revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the hit mainly to the war, which raised material and labour costs and caused panic buying and shortages; it said costs have stabilised and Q1 is expected to track the company's stated margin levels going forward.

qa_highlights.question: How many new projects in FY27 and what is the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: No guaranteed count; two to three development stages where the company is in the top three bidders, plus further tenders. Four pipeline projects with GDV above INR800 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Are Square and Signature margins tracking underwriting?
qa_highlights.answer: Slightly below, because materials were procured during the war; management said the impact should be minor over the remaining two to two-and-a-half year timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory status of ongoing projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Square about 80% sold; Signature about 50% (later 63-70%); Delight about 40%; Manorath 20-25%; Avenue and Icon only recently launched.

qa_highlights.question: How will capital employed and leverage be managed?
qa_highlights.answer: No leverage ceiling or capital-per-project framework set yet, as each project has different economics.

risks_watch: Margin recovery: Q1 EBITDA margin compression from war-related costs; watch whether Q2 margins return to the 20-30% range management cited.
Pipeline conversion: tenders are uncertain; Govind Dalvi is on hold due to a government stay on a 500-metre area.

Working capital and leverage: no framework yet for capital per project or leverage ceiling as project size rises.

Thin stock liquidity noted by an analyst; management attributed it to market conditions.

543547|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 13% and PAT reached INR202 crore (+9%); FY27 guidance is 2.31 lakh tonnes volume at 73% utilisation, with BESS excluded.
543547|2026-03.overview: Ddev Plastiks reported FY26 revenue up 13% YoY, EBITDA up 12% at an 11% margin, and PAT of INR202 crore (+9%). Volumes were 2,01,370 tonnes at 77% capacity utilisation, with exports up 30% and export volumes up 23%. Management said the Israel-Iran conflict from 28 February 2026 raised raw material costs by 50%-plus and briefly hurt demand, but supply and pricing have stabilised since April. guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR of 35-40% over three to five years, applied to the INR825 crore base; management said it is not revising guidance, with exact numbers to be shared during the year.
EBITDA margin for FY27 guided at 9-10%, described as 'closer to double digits'; management called 12% a wishful number.
PAT margin expected to improve by 50-100 bps over the next two years as Ind AS adjustments fade.
Compressor margin 6-7% in FY27, potentially above double digits over 2-4 years as Chinese imports restrict and backward integration rises (11-12% in 4-5 years).
RAC utilisation target of 60-65% and volume growth of about 30-40% in FY27.
Chennai plant expected to contribute about 5-6% of volume in its first year.
Peak-utilisation revenue capacity from the current expansion is good for beyond INR2,500 crore, but management said reaching that from INR800 crore in two years is a big ask and will take more time.
HoldCo net debt addition of about INR50-60 crore in FY27; INR150 crore debt at the compressor subsidiary; INR250 crore equity approval is a blanket enabling approval, not a fundraising commitment.
capex_capacity: Compressors: capacity 2.8 million to 6 million by March 2027 (9-10 month build), INR150 crore phase-1 investment, already tied up; long-term target 8-8.5 million, with 7.5 million or 9.5 million considered if demand and contracts materialise.
AC: capacity about 1 million to 1.8 million by end FY27, with 1.3 million targeted before the next AC season; investment INR40-50 crore, mainly debt-funded, with some debt already tied up.
EMS: new advanced facility; phase 1 by end-August 2026 and phase 2 by FY-end; investment about INR25 crore, tied up.

Government restricts reciprocating compressor imports to 40% of FY24-25 base-year levels, meaning 50-60% of OEM/ODM requirement must be sourced locally; the company says it is the only OEM/ODM player currently doing this.

Two competitors expected to start local compressor manufacturing (one by end-Q3/Q4 FY27, one mid-2027). Management estimates a market gap of 14-15 million units against total planned capacity of 15-18 million.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 revenue guidance lower than the INR1,200 crore target previously mentioned?

qa_highlights.question: Will the compressor capacity to 6 million be enough, and how does the QCO affect the 7.5 million plan?

Management kept FY27 guidance of 35-40% growth and 9-10% EBITDA margin, and said an upward revision depends on Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commercial refrigeration capex, revenue potential, and the medium-term CAPEX plan?

qa_highlights.question: What is the compressor margin trajectory, and how much is captive versus external?

543599|2026-03.headline: Ksolves FY26 revenue rose 18.4% to INR 162.7 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 29.7% from 34.8%; FY27 guided to 18-20% growth.
543599|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of INR 162.7 crore (up 18.4% YoY), EBITDA of INR 48.3 crore at a 29.7% margin, and PAT of INR 34.3 crore, flat with FY25. Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 43.03 crore (up 29.1% YoY, 1.7% QoQ) with a 29.3% EBITDA margin and PAT of INR 9.7 crore. Margin compression was attributed to planned investments in ESOPs, leadership, travel and events, DFM product development, and a one-time INR 1.1 crore labour-code impact. For FY27, management guided to 18-20% revenue growth and a 25-30% EBITDA margin, and said it is shifting focus fully to IT services and winding down product spend.

segments.name: IT services
segments.commentary: Core revenue and profit driver; services span ERP, cloud, data, AI, Salesforce and enterprise transformation. Management says 82% of revenue is recurring.

segments.name: Product (DFM)
segments.commentary: Small contributor. About INR 2 crore expensed on DFM development in FY26; two customers sold to, with two or three in pipeline now pushed to June/July. Management says no further big DFM development spend in FY27 and event spend to fall at least 60%.

FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 25% to 30%; management aspires to finish at the higher end.
FY26 expense increases (ESOPs, leadership pay, travel/events, DFM, labour-code one-time INR 1.1 crore) described as largely non-recurring.
Dividend payout to continue at 40% to 60% of profits, as no acquisitions are planned in the coming quarters.
Shift toward more fixed-price and outcome-based engagements and continued talent investment in FY27.
capex_capacity: No capacity or capex figures were disclosed on the call.
DFM product development considered complete; no further large DFM investment planned in FY27.
Added ERPNext/Frappe partnership alongside Odoo to broaden ERP offering; installed-base metrics to be shared later by IR.
Multiple specialist data-science resources added for a US-based financial-crime client, supplied as dedicated people rather than employees.
demand_pricing: Q4 growth was held back by delayed POs from UAE customers due to the ongoing war; management said orders are now being released.
Management said deal conversions are strong and demand healthy, though some deals have been delayed.
Clients are migrating from SAP to Odoo to cut costs; a Tanzanian prospect was cited as a further example.
Management said pricing pressure from AI was not the reason for margin decline; no price-cut detail was given.
Management did not give a order-book or pipeline figure when asked.

qa_highlights.question: How much efficiency will AI agents bring to employee costs in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not measured it yet; agents are reducing time and raising output, and agents are being built for repetitive tasks.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins recover given the marketing and ESOP costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Costs are described as non-recurring, with some expenses continuing at lower scale; Q4 margin was at the upper end of the guided range and is expected to hold.

qa_highlights.question: Why was DFM product spend not converting, and is there further hope?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said expectations were higher than customer acceptance; it sold to two customers, sees limited DFM opportunity, and will focus on services.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide to a wide 25-30% margin band and why slower growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is being conservative given geopolitical uncertainty, and that the larger revenue base means the same percentage adds more absolute revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Are UAE war-related delays affecting orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; some UAE customers delayed orders, holding Q4 QoQ growth to 1.7%, and POs are now being released.

qa_highlights.question: Will PAT grow faster than revenue in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited heavy AI, insurance and IT security investment, so the 25-30% margin band is kept; the aspiration is to end at the higher end.

543599|2026-06.headline: Ksolves Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 41.4 crore, but management withdrew FY27 revenue guidance while EBITDA margin hit 30.3%.

Management said it would not reaffirm FY27 revenue guidance, now expecting flat-to-4-5% growth at most, and reiterated a 25-30% EBITDA margin range. The company remains debt-free and declared an interim dividend of Rs 4 per share.

543599|2026-09.headline: Ksolves Q2 FY27 revenue fell 4.7% YoY to INR 37.8 crores on client ramp-downs; EBITDA margin 25.7%, within guided band.
543599|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 37.8 crores, down 4.7% YoY and 8.8% QoQ, driven by client-specific ramp-downs at a couple of large enterprise accounts and cautious client spending. EBITDA was INR 9.7 crores at a 25.7% margin (vs 30.3% in Q1 and 30.4% in Q2 FY26), which management attributed to lower revenue partly offset by cost actions and AI-led productivity. PAT was INR 7.25 crores (19.2% margin), and H1 revenue grew 2.5% YoY to INR 79.2 crores. Management guided FY27 revenue to trail FY26 and EBITDA margin to stay within 25-30%, with H2 focus on pipeline building, AI opportunities and enterprise account recovery.

financial_highlights.change: vs 30.3% in Q1 FY27 and 30.4% in Q2 FY26
broadly in line with H1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR 1 per share second interim; H1 total INR 5 per share (~72% of H1 PAT)

segments.name: IT services
segments.commentary: Core business at 98.4% of Q2 revenue. Geography: North America 59%, India 20%, Europe 6%, Australia 4%, rest of world 11%; overseas 80%.

segments.name: BFSI / banking
segments.commentary: Three Q2 wins in banking (South America, UK, Europe). BFSI share of revenue rose from 7% to 8% (H1 FY26 vs H1 FY27 per analyst slide); management says the jump comes from H2. Company has about 11-12 BFSI clients.

segments.name: Telecom
segments.commentary: Largest segment at about 25% of revenue this year vs 27% last year per analyst reading of slides; one telecom client that was closing its business is now re-engaging.

Being a Select Partner in Anthropic (Claude) and OpenAI networks; 100% of engineers Claude certified.
demand_pricing: Client spending remains selective and discretionary spend under scrutiny; management said clients had put decisions on hold until around 10 September over AI wait-and-watch, and are now returning with AI-led requirements.
Customers now ask for Odoo, Salesforce or data engineering with agentic AI; management says the sales question has shifted from headcount to business outcome.
Two large enterprise accounts ramped down; management called these client-specific, not structural, and said the pipeline was not deep enough to offset them in the quarter.
Management said some clients tested building in-house AI tools but have since returned to outsourcing projects for features.
Top 10 clients contributed 50% of revenue.

qa_highlights.answer: No, the company is not currently calculating revenue in constant currency.

qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number, but said it was large enough to be a big hit; new Q1 and Q2 wins absorbed much of it, though a deficit remained.

qa_highlights.question: How will the margin move with sales traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins would be at the upper end of the guided range if revenue recovers; the INR 3.6 crore revenue drop was the main driver of the Q2 margin dip.

qa_highlights.question: Will the banking wins contribute meaningfully, and how big can BFSI become?
qa_highlights.answer: Projects are underway and take months to quarters; the South American bank relationship is ongoing but expansion is not in writing. Management hopes other banks will follow.

qa_highlights.answer: Still exploring; management sees AI guardrails and security as a demand opportunity but has not defined the offering.

543600|2026-03.headline: Harsha Engineers Q4 FY26 Engineering EBITDA rose to INR77 crore; FY26 Engineering revenue INR1,444 crore, guided to double-digit FY27 growth.
543600|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 consolidated Engineering revenue of INR382 crore and EBITDA of INR77 crore, versus adjusted EBITDA of INR64.3 crore in Q3 and INR66 crore in Q4 FY25. For FY26, Engineering revenue grew to INR1,444 crore from INR1,269 crore, with consolidated EBITDA of INR264 crore (about INR270 crore adjusted for the new Labour Code impact). Solar revenue was INR183 crore with PAT of INR10.2 crore. Management guided to double-digit FY27 consolidated growth, with India Engineering in the mid-teens, and to maintaining current margins. The call also covered weak Romania profitability, the Advantek ramp-up, and the China steel-cage expansion.

vs adjusted INR64.3 crore in Q3 FY26 and INR66 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.change: PAT INR10.2 crore vs adjusted PAT INR5 crore in FY25

segments.commentary: Revenue INR127 crore in FY26, up about 25%, driven by design conversion in wind planetary gearboxes from bearings to bushings. Management targets 25-30% growth in FY27.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR60 crore. Growth drivers are AC compressor components and white goods. Management expects at least 20% growth next year and 15-20% mid-term.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR183 crore with PAT INR10.2 crore. Q4 revenue about INR91 crore, roughly doubled YoY. Management expects more than 25% growth and Solar EBITDA margin to hold near the FY26 level.

segments.commentary: Still at low utilisation; FY26 EBITDA INR4 crore but net loss about INR11 crore on depreciation and interest. Sales expected to grow at least 3x in FY27; current installed capacity seen generating INR250-300 crore turnover.

segments.commentary: FY26 turnover about INR120 crore, PAT about INR5 crore profit. Brownfield steel-cage expansion to be commissioned in H2 FY28; INR70 crore capex in FY27 and INR20 crore in FY28.

segments.commentary: FY26 turnover about INR247 crore with PAT loss about INR14 crore. Cage share of mix at about 22%, targeted to rise to 30-35%. Wind market in Europe not yet recovered.

Management indicated the India-level business could reach INR2,400-2,500 crore and consolidated INR2,700-3,000 crore on current capabilities, depending on capacity additions.

Management said the Advantek capex includes infrastructure that will not translate immediately into fixed-asset-to-revenue multiples.
Saket Kapoor noted PP&E closing balance of about INR615 crore.
demand_pricing: Export growth of about 17% in FY26 was attributed to improving European and US industrial markets; US import tariff on cages was cut to zero, aiding US picks-up.

Pass-through of raw-material costs (steel, brass, metal prices) to customers is contractual, with an average lag of about four months. Q4 growth was mainly volume-driven, as metal prices moved mainly from late December to February/March.

Europe demand is improving slowly, but management said there is no definitive recovery and that cost and pricing issues remain. Europe is about 30% of sales, China just over 10%, US 6-7% and Japan about 2%.
Domestic bearing makers are ramping capacity and are expected to invest further; management is bullish, though it flagged risks from the war and petroleum prices.
Cost pressure is building from oils, lubricants and plastic cage material; logistics has not been impacted so far. Management is working to mitigate or pass through these costs.
Management said wallet share is about 70-90% in India but only 10-20% with large overseas customers and 2-3% with the Japan-based customer.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 27% consolidated growth was mainly Solar; Engineering grew 15.7% YoY. Growth was mostly volume-led, and pass-through is automatic with an average lag of about four months.

qa_highlights.answer: China: turnover about INR120 crore with PAT about INR5 crore profit. Romania: turnover about INR247 crore with PAT loss about INR14 crore. Combined subsidiary loss was INR9 crore after correction; management said losses would reduce significantly.

qa_highlights.answer: Europe is slowly improving, with no sharp recovery. Restructuring is ongoing, the cost structure is not yet right, and Romania still has negative margins. Management is evaluating how long it can sustain these margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: India maintenance capex of INR30-40 crore per year; China expansion INR70 crore in FY27 and INR20 crore in FY28; further Advantek phase-two capex is being finalised.

qa_highlights.question: What is Advantek's ramp-up timeline and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Current installed capacity expected to peak in about two years, with turnover of INR250-300 crore. Expansion beyond that is planned.

qa_highlights.question: What drives bushing growth and what is the stamping outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Bushing growth comes from design conversion in wind planetary gearboxes away from bearings. Stampings (about INR60 crore in FY26) are driven by AC compressor and white goods components; management expects at least 20% growth next year.

543600|2026-06.headline: Harsha Engineers Q1 FY27 consolidated Engineering supply up 25% YoY to Rs 421 crore, but EBITDA margin compressed on a 6-7% raw material spike pending pass-through.
543600|2026-06.overview: Consolidated Engineering supply rose to Rs 421 crore from Rs 382 crore QoQ and Rs 349 crore YoY, with India Engineering growing about 21% YoY and 6% QoQ. Consolidated Engineering EBITDA was Rs 69.8 crore versus Rs 77 crore QoQ and Rs 65.3 crore YoY, so margin fell QoQ. Management attributed the squeeze to an ~8% rise in average raw material cost (lagged pass-through of one to two quarters), about Rs 4 crore of FX hedge accounting loss, and about Rs 3 crore of higher indirect material costs after the West Asia conflict. Management kept FY27 guidance of high-teens India growth and low-teens consolidated growth, with India Engineering EBITDA margin of 22-24%.

qa_highlights.question: Was the growth broad-based across segments, and was it driven by Europe or India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was broad-based, with industrial demand strengthening in India and European demand recovering. It called 20% FY27 consolidated growth a very tough stretch and expects mid-to-high-teens India growth and low-teens consolidated growth.

qa_highlights.question: Which raw materials drove the cost increase, and how is foreign EBITDA margin trending?
qa_highlights.answer: The RM increase spans brass, copper, zinc, steel and polymer, not just brass as last year. On foreign subsidiaries, management said it is trying to shift to cages, while the raw material spike and FX offset the revenue gains. Management did not quantify the margin decline.

qa_highlights.question: How large are the Romania losses, and is the subsidiary restructuring on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Romania did not significantly improve ex-FX and copper prices hurt results. Sanjay Majmudar guided combined China and Romania loss of about Rs 2-3 crore for FY27 versus about Rs 10 crore last year, with Romania possibly profitable next year.

qa_highlights.question: Are bushing and stamping growth sustainable, and is large-cage growth credible after a weak Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Bushing growth is driven by conversion and wallet share, with conversion expected to support growth for at least a couple of years. Stamping growth comes from new products maturing over about one year. Large-cage Q1 was about Rs 10 crore due to ramp-up constraints at the new facility, and management still expects about 30-50% growth, citing order book and pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CapEx outlook for FY27 and FY28, and what is the Bhayla status?
qa_highlights.answer: China Phase-2 is on track for Q3 FY28 commissioning. Bhayla building construction was delayed by heavy rain and expected to start this month, with the third building targeted for completion by end-2026 or Q4 FY27. Annual CapEx is guided at Rs 50-80 crore, with Rs 180-200 crore over 1.5-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: How much of India growth is volume versus price, and what price increase is being taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth is the focus and the price impact is not being predicted. Maulik Jasani estimated the 6-7% RM increase would lift selling prices by about 40-50% of that, roughly 3-4%. The Japanese customer was Rs 21 crore in Q1 versus Rs 16.5 crore a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Advantek EBITDA and margin expectations, and what is the normal India Engineering margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Advantek Q1 EBITDA margin was about 9%, and it is expected to be slightly below the India blended margin in FY27, matching it from FY28. Vishal Rangwala said the 24% Q1 standalone margin is high and a normal sustainable margin is 20-22%. Jason Soans's question on the 22-24% guidance was answered by Maulik Jasani, who said margin percentage will fall as pass-through lifts realisations.

543619|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue from operations INR 210.47 crore with PAT INR 42.7 crore and executable order book of about INR 697 crore, 3.3x FY26 revenue.
543619|2026-03.overview: Management (Joint MD Gaurav Lath) framed Concord as evolving from a railway equipment maker into a full-stack railway technology and lifecycle platform, built on four pillars: green mobility, smart locomotive intelligence, railway safety (Kavach/MSDAC), and AI-driven diagnostics. FY26 figures stated were revenue from operations INR 210.47 crore, PAT INR 42.7 crore, EBITDA INR 62.1 crore, and an executable order book of about INR 697 crore at 31 March 2026. Working capital was the main analyst concern: receivables and short-term debt rose sharply, which management attributed to back-ended railway billing in Q4 and said will persist through the growth phase. Several questions on Fusion Electronics revenue, Kavach tender outcomes and loco-Kavach opportunity size got non-committal answers.

segments.name: Locomotive solutions
segments.commentary: Management said locomotive solutions are currently the larger contributor to growth, including DPWCS (distributed power wireless control systems). No segment-wise revenue split was given.

segments.name: Kavach / railway safety (via Progota)
segments.commentary: Field trials started; management hopes for a successful year. Trial completion and ISA approval are targeted within FY27. Kavach pillar is positioned as large and long-duration, with no revenue figure given.

segments.name: Green mobility

Management did not confirm the analyst's figure of about 17,000 loco units tendered; it said the total loco population is 13,000 to 16,000 including train sets and MEMUs.
No direct response on whether the LNG and geopolitical crisis could slow railway spending, beyond general references to uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise sharply, and will this working capital pattern continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to back-ended Q4 billing and customer acceptance cycles with railways. Said receivable cycles had improved by June versus last year, and confirmed similar working capital will recur.

qa_highlights.question: How should debt and balance sheet strength be seen over the next few years, given short-term debt rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 is always heavier and working capital will spike with the INR 697 crore order book, then ease. It declined to give peak debt estimates.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% to 25% EBITDA guidance conservative given around 30% in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims for realistic guidance and that technology adoption is faster than expected, without accepting the conservatism framing.

qa_highlights.question: When will operating cash flow turn positive, and is there any liquidity challenge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said railway payments are streamlined and sovereign-backed with no penalty or bad-debt risk, and that cash flow will not deter growth. Confirmed that some money started coming in from April, but gave no timeline for positive operating cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company face penalties for delayed order execution, and will it grow execution faster than 40% to 50%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company executed similar growth last year and planned more structured execution for the large order book. No penalty figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue can Fusion Electronics deliver this year, and why has it shown little revenue so far?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a turnaround with a typical 300-day integration cycle and said full-scale revenue could be about INR 200 crore. It expects revenue contribution this year.

qa_highlights.question: How will Kavach orders be executed, and when will the 4,500-unit loco Kavach tender be decided?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kavach orders have two to three phases (production, inspection, installation), with part of the invoice paid on delivery and the balance after installation. The tender outcome timing was not given; it said finalisation is a process.

543620|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 61% to INR2,146 crore and PAT 59% to INR201 crore; cell line guided to lift EBITDA margin toward 20%+ later.
543620|2026-03.overview: Insolation Energy listed on BSE and NSE Main Board on 9 March 2026. FY26 revenue from operations was INR2,146 crore (up 61%), EBITDA INR305 crore (up 79%, margin 14% vs 13%), and PAT INR201 crore (up 59%). Q4 FY26 revenue was INR794 crore (up 100% YoY), with EBITDA INR111 crore and PAT INR70 crore, though management said utility-scale dispatches cluster in the last month of each quarter. Management is building a 4.5 GW TOPCon cell line and 4.5 GW aluminium frame plant at Narmadapuram, with cell COD targeted for Q3/Q4 FY27 and frames in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did December and March not sustain the run rate of Q4 revenue?

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital and debt picture after receivables rose 156%?

rows.why: Aluminium frame plant (4.5 GW) due to commission in Q1 FY27 and the 4.5 GW TOPCon cell line is under construction with INR340 crore drawn from IREDA by 31 March 2026 and ramp-up expected in Q4 FY27, though the brief notes the cell line timing is still forward-looking.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets about 2 GW module production and sales in FY27 versus the FY26 base, with FY27 revenue growth guided at least 50-60%, backed by a 1.6-1.8 GW order book and about 50% of FY27 capacity already booked.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex guided at about INR2,500 crore (INR1,500 crore cell line, INR1,000 crore KUSUM IPP), and a 4.5 GW ingot/wafer plant (INR1,000-1,200 crore) has a DPR due in 2-3 months with 20 acres of land still remaining at Narmadapuram.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said FY27 margins could be revised upward if market conditions allow, with the order book at 1.6-1.8 GW and about 50% of FY27 capacity (about 2 GW) already booked.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raw-material cost inflation is mostly USD-linked with only 2-3 months of inventory cover, next two quarters' utilisation is guided at only 60-70%, and the cell line ramp timing (Q4 FY27 start) carries execution risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Q1 FY27 (aluminium frames); Q3/Q4 FY27 (TOPCon cells)
rows.why: The 4.5 GW aluminium frame plant is due in Q1 FY27 mainly for internal use, and the 4.5 GW TOPCon cell line targets COD in Q3/Q4 FY27 with cell efficiency target above 80%.

rows.label: Peak debt near INR1,500 crore then FCF positive
rows.when: FY27 peak; positive FCF 6-8 months after cell plant goes liv
rows.why: Total borrowings rose to INR835 crore from INR108 crore a year earlier, peak debt is guided near INR1,500 crore in FY27, and the CFO expects positive free cash flow 6-8 months after cell plant COD, though FCFF yield is cited at -15.9% until then.

rows.label: FY28 revenue above INR5,000 crore
rows.why: Management targets FY28 revenue above INR5,000 crore versus FY26 INR2,146 crore, which depends on the cell line ramp and market conditions, with IPP revenue guided at about INR300 crore in FY28.

rows.label: Receivables and quarter-end loading
rows.why: Trade receivables rose 156% YoY to INR280 crore as orders moved to 45-day LCs and dispatches cluster in the last month of each quarter (about INR350 crore in December and INR440 crore in March).

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term growth, the frame plant and the cell line, and on margins of 20%+ in FY28, but hedged near-term figures against market conditions; analysts and the brief flagged inconsistency on FY27 margin and capex funding, and several questions were re-asked.

543626|2026-03.headline: Electronics Mart Q4 FY26 revenue rose 15% to INR1,913 crores and SSSG hit 12.2%, with EBITDA margin up to 6.7%.
543626|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 15% YoY to INR1,913 crores, with EBITDA up 20% to INR129 crores and margin expanding to 6.7% from 5.6%. Same-store sales growth was 12.2% in the quarter, helped by GST rate cuts, festive demand and mobile launches, while FY26 SSSG was 5.3%. FY26 revenue rose 7% to INR7,183 crores with EBITDA of INR438 crores (6.1% margin) and PAT of INR107 crores. Management said working capital requirements have fallen and pre Ind AS operating cash flow reached INR299 crores for the year.

segments.name: South cluster (AP, Telangana, Hyderabad)
segments.commentary: Management cites a 6.5% EBITDA margin for the South cluster, with about INR6,000-6,500 crores of revenue from the region (69 AP stores, 46 Telangana, 72 Hyderabad city). Hyderabad city generated about INR4,122 crores in FY26; Hyderabad SSSG was double-digit in Q4.

segments.name: North cluster (NCR/Delhi)
segments.commentary: Delhi NCR operates 35 stores with about INR590 crores of revenue in FY26 and is now EBITDA positive on a full-year basis. Management guided to 25-30% growth in FY27 and a 2.5-3% EBITDA margin, versus about 0.2-0.3% now; Q4 Delhi like-to-like sales were reported at about 19%.

segments.name: Mature vs new stores
segments.commentary: Of 223 stores, 83 are over 4 years old (about 7.3% EBITDA margin) and 140 are under 4 years old (about 3.1% margin).

segments.name: Product categories
segments.commentary: Panels grew 13% and mobile phones 28% in Q4; washing machines grew strongly in double digits, refrigerators were stable, and large appliance mix fell from 47% to 42%.

guidance_outlook: Organic store additions of about 20 in FY27 (12-15 in NCR and AP/Telangana per management, plus Delhi and South openings), with capex of about INR3-4 crores per store assumed for 8,000-10,000 sq ft stores.
New East entry starting with 5-7 stores in Kolkata by end-Q2 or start-Q3 FY27; FY27 real estate spend of about INR50 crores, up to INR100 crores over 12-14 months.

NCR revenue target of INR800+ crores in FY27 (vs INR585 crores in FY26), with 2-4% EBITDA margin; Andhra Pradesh (INR1,100+ crores) and Telangana (INR1,000 crores) expected to deliver higher single-digit SSSG.
North cluster margin to be 3-4% higher than now by FY28 (not stated as an exact level).
Management expects ASPs up at least 5-6% on average in FY26 with volume held; price hikes are passed through to customers; inventory to be bought 2-3% higher at newer prices for the next 20 days.
capex_capacity: Store count 223 (83 over 4 years old, 140 under 4 years); Q4 added 4 stores (NCR, Telangana, 2 in Andhra Pradesh).
Management plans 12-15 organic stores in NCR, AP and Telangana, with 4-5 Delhi stores getting ready, and 7-8 more stores in NCR; new Kolkata cluster to start with 5-7 stores by end-Q2 or start-Q3.
Store size 8,000-10,000 sq ft typical, capex about INR3-4 crores per store, similar product mix in new regions.
Working capital requirement reduced; cash flow prioritised over expansion, with loans against property repaid organically.
Franchise model not in use; all stores company-operated, with franchising only to be explored if OEMs support it.
demand_pricing: Q4 demand robust across categories; washing machines grew strongly in double digits, panels 13%, mobile phones 28% (new launches in January and March).
ASPs rose at least 5-6% on average in FY26 for the same volume (bigger TV sizes after GST cut, higher-star ACs), and management says no category saw ASP decline.
Price hikes on RAC products of about INR1,500-2,000 per SKU are passed on to customers; additional inventory bought at 2-3% higher prices.
Entry-level mobile price hikes (below INR20,000) have limited impact, as the company's mobile ASP is about INR35,000-40,000.
Sourcing is essentially direct from OEMs/brands; distributor purchases are about INR50 crores a year, with margins unchanged.
Competition: NCR faces Croma, Reliance and Vijay Sales; South competes mostly with mom-and-pop stores, which drives the margin gap.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Hyderabad SSSG double-digit in Q4 and how should FY27 be read?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to the GST cut benefit across categories (TVs, washing machines, dishwashers, refrigerators, cooling products) plus mobile launches; early Q1 trends were good.

qa_highlights.question: How did gross margin hold up as large appliance mix fell from 47% to 42%?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins were supported by higher-margin categories (mobile accessories, built-in appliances, audio) and better throughput; management expects margins to hold or improve.

qa_highlights.question: Store opening cadence and cash flow deployment?
qa_highlights.answer: Store openings slowed as Delhi was a new market in FY25; Hyderabad adds only 1-2 stores a year. Management said cash is reinvested, working capital has fallen and loans are repaid organically.

qa_highlights.question: Delhi/NCR margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets INR800+ crores revenue and 2-4% EBITDA margin in FY27, with a 3-4% higher margin than now by FY28; the NCR cluster is EBITDA positive for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: Franchise model?
qa_highlights.answer: No franchising currently; management said it would consider franchising only in a region where OEM support and partner alignment exist, citing seasonality and consumer experience.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter Kolkata while NCR is still stabilising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Delhi stabilisation is done and growth will be organic; Kolkata is a new cluster with a 12-14 month learning cycle, starting with 5-7 stores by end-Q2 or start-Q3.

risks_watch: Delhi/NCR execution: Q4 growth was off a low base, and management targets 25-30% growth and a 2.5-3% margin in FY27 from a 0.2-0.3% base.
Summer and cooling demand: Delhi started late, and about 50% of Q1 remained at the time of the call; cooling products are key to the quarter's margin.
Store maturity: 140 stores under 4 years old run at 3.1% margin versus 7.3% for mature stores.
Working capital and inventory: inventory days were 73 at 31 March 2026; RAC inventory was bought at older prices, with more purchases at higher prices expected.
Kolkata entry is new and capital-intensive (up to INR100 crores of real estate over 12-14 months).
543626|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on South/Hyderabad and the margin trajectory, but more measured on Delhi, where management said growth will be more organic. Some answers were evasive on volume-versus-value splits and on Q1 trends.
key_quotes: We also saw a meaningful operating leverage coming through, resulting in an improvement in our operating margins, even as we continue to add new stores to our network.
Mature stores continue to demonstrate strong performance with an EBITDA margin of approximately 7.3%, while newer stores are currently operating at 3.1%, consistent with their stage of ramp-up.
So Calcutta would be a new base for East.

rows.why: Management expects FY27 SSSG of higher single digits in AP (INR1,100+ crore) and Telangana (INR1,000 crore), NCR revenue of INR800+ crore vs INR585 crore in FY26 (+25-30%), and ~20 new stores added, though FY26 SSSG was 5.3% with ASP up 5-6% and volume held.

rows.why: Management says cash is prioritised over expansion, working capital has fallen, and loans against property are being repaid organically; no utilisation data was given and no new capex beyond the planned store and Kolkata programme was flagged.

rows.why: Q4 SSSG was 12.2% with Hyderabad double-digit and early Q1 trends described as good, but the GST-cut and mobile-launch benefits may fade and management was evasive on Q1 trends.

rows.why: NCR needs 25-30% growth to reach INR800+ crore and a 2-4% margin from a 0.2-0.3% base, and Delhi started summer late with about 50% of Q1 still open at the time of the call.

rows.why: No specific new product or brand launch was guided; mobile launches in January and March drove a 28% Q4 mobile growth but were not framed as a forward pipeline.

rows.why: Pre Ind AS operating cash flow reached INR299 crore in FY26 and loans against property are being repaid organically, with inventory at 73 days on 31 March 2026.

rows.why: 5-7 stores guided in Kolkata with about INR50 crore real estate spend in FY27, rising to INR100 crore over 12-14 months.

rows.why: Price hikes of INR1,500-2,000 per SKU on RAC are passed to customers, with inventory bought 2-3% higher and FY26 ASP up at least 5-6% at unchanged volume.

543626|2026-06.headline: Electronics Mart Q1 FY27 revenue rose 39% to INR 2,419 crore and PAT to INR 121 crore, with reported EBITDA margin at 9.9%.
543626|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the company's strongest quarter to date, driven by a strong AC season, healthy footfalls and conversions, and 34.2% same-store sales growth. Gross margin expanded to 17.2% from 14.6%, aided by cooling-product mix and temporary price-increase gains in IT hardware. Working capital days fell to 42 from 73 and working capital borrowings dropped to INR 97 crore from INR 658 crore at the start of the quarter. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 18-20% and a post-Ind AS EBITDA margin of 7.5-8%, and said the margin tailwinds are partly temporary.

segments.name: Large appliances
segments.commentary: 48% of revenue, led by air conditioners, with traction in washing machines and refrigerators. AC season was the best quarter yet by volume and value.

segments.name: Mobile phones
segments.commentary: 39% of revenue in Q1 FY27, down from 40% in the comparable base, as cooling-product mix rose seasonally.

segments.name: South cluster
segments.commentary: Revenue +40% YoY with EBITDA margin of 10.9%. Andhra Pradesh revenue +62% (SSG 49.1%), Telangana up-country +48% (SSG 40%), Hyderabad city +34% (SSG 32.3%).

segments.name: North cluster
segments.commentary: Revenue +29% YoY with record EBITDA margin of 4.9%. Management said North market for cooling products was negative versus 2024.

segments.name: Store maturity
segments.commentary: 96 stores older than 4 years run at 11.2% EBITDA margin; 131 stores under 4 years old delivered 8.1%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 18-20% YoY, described as 'very easily achievable'; upside possible if Q4 season is strong. Management declined to commit to INR 10,000 crore revenue.
FY27 full-year gross margin guided at 15-15.5%, below the Q1 level, as Q1 benefited from temporary price-increase gains.
Post-Ind AS EBITDA margin guided at 7.5-8% for FY27; management called 9% 'too optimistic'.
Finance cost expected to be at least INR 10 crore lower than last year's ~INR 150 crore.
Plan to open 25-30 stores in FY27 across existing geographies and West Bengal; 5 Kolkata stores by Diwali and 10-12 by end-Q4 FY27; 8-10 NCR stores in FY27 and about 5 South stores.
West Bengal capex about INR 100 crore for stores plus about INR 50 crore for property purchases over the next two years, funded from internal accruals.
risks_watch: Gross margin tailwind from temporary price-increase gains in laptops and mobiles may reverse; management guides FY27 gross margin to 15-15.5%.
Delhi NCR same-store sales weak as North cooling-product market declined; management expects improvement but gave no quarterly figures.
Memory-chip shortages may force higher stock levels (50-60 days instead of 30) for some IT and mobile SKUs.
Management could not quantify the share of inventory bought at lower prior-year cost, so the gross margin benefit is hard to isolate.
Quality of the Q1 base: the comparison is against a weak AC season in Q1 FY26, so the growth rate may not persist.
New store ramp in West Bengal and North; execution against 25-30 openings a year and the 10-12 Kolkata target by March 2027.

financial_highlights.change: +458% YoY (vs INR 22 crore); highest ever quarterly profit
vs INR 658 crore at start of quarter

financial_highlights.value: INR 631 crore (pre-Ind AS), INR 671 crore (post-Ind AS)

qa_highlights.question: What are full-year FY27 revenue and gross margin targets, given the weak base?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth of 18-20% is described as very easily achievable; management declined to commit to INR 10,000 crore. FY27 gross margin guided at 15-15.5%, with Q1's 17.2% partly temporary from price-increase gains.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin expansion and is the benefit sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher cooling-product mix and buying laptops and mobiles at lower prices during price rises; it called the price-increase gain temporary and could not quantify the low-cost inventory share.

qa_highlights.question: Is post-Ind AS EBITDA margin at 8-9% achievable and what is the finance cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said 9% is too optimistic and 7.5-8% is easily achievable; finance cost to be at least INR 10 crore lower than last year's ~INR 150 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Delhi NCR SSG weak and what store openings are planned there and in Kolkata?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the North cooling market declined versus 2024 and the base was small; Kolkata has 5 stores by Diwali and 10-12 by March 2027; NCR 8-10 stores this year.

qa_highlights.question: Capex requirement for West Bengal and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 100 crore for stores plus about INR 50 crore for property purchases over two years, all funded from internal accruals; about 30 stores in Kolkata over 24 months.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company quantify its market share gains and volume versus price contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Market share gains estimated at 4% to 12% outside Hyderabad depending on the geography; growth attributed mainly to volume, with ASP up only in limited categories.

capex_capacity: Plans 25-30 store openings in FY27 across existing geographies and West Bengal; 5 Kolkata stores operational by Diwali and 10-12 by 31 March 2027; 8-10 NCR stores this financial year (two opening that week in Saket and Gurgaon, 3-4 under construction); about 5 South stores.

West Bengal capex of about INR 100 crore (plus or minus INR 5-10 crore) for stores plus about INR 50 crore for buying about 11 properties in Kolkata over the next two years, transactions possibly in Q1-Q2 FY28; all funded from internal accruals.

Per-store economics: about INR 2,500 per sq ft capex on a 10,000 sq ft store (about INR 2.5 crore) plus about INR 2 crore inventory; payback under 10-11 months in South and 16-18 months in North; breakeven 30-40 days in South and about 2-2.5 months in North.
Store opex targets: rent under 3% of revenue initially, manpower and marketing each under 1%, total store opex 8-10%; SSG targeted at 10-12% from year three.
Management said it will not commit to inorganic or rapid expansion and no franchise model; all stores are company-owned and company-operated on leased properties.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 SSG 34.2%; South cluster revenue +40% with 10.9% EBITDA margin; Andhra Pradesh revenue +62% (SSG 49.1%), Telangana up-country +48% (SSG 40%), Hyderabad city +34% (SSG 32.3%).
North cluster revenue +29% with 4.9% EBITDA margin; management said the North cooling-product market declined versus 2024, and Delhi NCR SSG was weak.

Management said the Andhra Pradesh AC unit volume was about 26,000-27,000 in the first six months against about 20,000 a year earlier with a similar store count; claimed market share gains of 4% to 12% in existing clusters outside Hyderabad.

Price gains were concentrated in laptops and mobiles due to chipset/memory shortages; TVs, refrigerators, washing machines and ACs saw single-digit price hikes. Gains were periodic, not across all brands or the full 90 days.
Bill cuts grew about 36% while ASP grew about 2%, per an analyst's read; management attributed this to volume growth and low-ticket accessories and audio.

Mobile share fell to 39% from 40% on seasonal cooling-product mix; management expects mix to normalise by year-end within 1-2%. Management expects the North to trend toward South margins as stores mature.
Management said it expects memory-chip shortages may require 50-60 days stock instead of 30 days for some IT and mobile SKUs, not across all categories.
key_quotes: I am delighted to share that Q1 FY27 has been our strongest quarter to date with all the key metrics moving decisively in the right direction.
But that is a temporary upside.
It will be too optimistic. 9% means too optimistic.
So no inorganic expansion, no rapid expansion. It will be all calculated.
