543638|2026-03.headline: Tracxn Q4 FY26 revenue from operations Rs 20.5 crore; EBITDA negative Rs 6.6 crore, PAT marginally negative Rs 0.6 crore, adjusted PAT positive Rs 2.5 crore.
543638|2026-03.overview: Tracxn reported Q4 FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 20.5 crore, with EBITDA negative at Rs 6.6 crore and PAT marginally negative at Rs 0.6 crore after non-cash ESOP charges. Management said FY26 revenue was Rs 84 crore and that Q4 volume growth accelerated, with paid customers rising 19% YoY to 2,289. Management described the deal environment as weak in deal volume (near a 10-year low) while M&A and IB activity was rebounding, and it is adding GTM headcount and AI distribution channels for FY27. Blended ASP per account fell, driven mainly by mix shift toward lower-priced accounts rather than price cuts.

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted EBITDA (excluding non-cash ESOP), Q4 FY26

segments.name: Paid customer base by type
segments.commentary: About 49% of paid customers are investment-side (VC, PE, banks, family offices, accelerators, incubators) and 46% corporates; 55% of revenue is from outside India. Top five markets are US, UK, Singapore, Germany.

segments.name: Investment banking (IB) customers
segments.commentary: IB customer count up 20% YoY and IB ASP up 40% YoY per management; banks segment logo penetration rising month on month.

segments.name: Academic and universities
segments.commentary: Academic customer count up 55% and revenue up 60% YoY; IIMs, IITs, ISB and XLRI among customers; five of top six IIMs are customers.

guidance_outlook: GTM (sales) headcount to be doubled from 25 to 40 by end of calendar 2026, with a further closing target of 60 by December 2026 per management's plan; sales-team share of headcount at 30% versus 23% in FY25.
Major product investments planned for FY27 in US and Europe valuation, CXO datasets, and legal-entity coverage; partner-led uptake expected from Q1 FY27.
Management expects strong M&A/IB momentum, with 2026 YTD M&A deal value possibly the highest since the 2021 peak.

Management said the company is geared up for FY27 but gave no explicit margin or revenue guidance; it indicated margins can expand non-linearly as revenue re-accelerates, with historical conversion of up to 80% of incremental revenue to bottom line.
Management said it is eligible for a buyback or dividend once accumulated losses are cleared, but gave no decision timeline.
capex_capacity: Cloud hosting is the largest cost item at 3.1 crore of expenses in the quarter, reflecting heavy data processing; rent is the next largest; no paid digital or offline acquisition spend, with content generated in-house.
Total headcount is entirely in-house with no outsourced or contract workforce; ops headcount reportedly shrank about 20% through automation.
Employee expense as a share of revenue historically 5-10% of expenses; management expects it to rise and stay in a higher range as the GTM team is added.
demand_pricing: Blended ASP per account fell from about Rs 5 lakh to about Rs 4 lakh per account per year; management attributed this to mix shift toward lower-priced accounts, not list-price cuts.
Deal volume in venture funding remains near a 10-year low, while dollars invested improved; late-stage funding weak.
M&A and IB activity rebounding; management said 2026 could be among the highest years since the 2021 peak by M&A deal value.
Partnership pipeline: TMX partnership in pilot with no meaningful revenue yet; enterprise partner deals take one to two quarters to launch.
Launched a Claude connector (MCP) and an AI chat assistant in beta; management sees AI platforms as a new distribution channel, with no revenue contribution yet.
Metered and individual report purchases launched; management described this as small and expected to grow.
Paid acquisition is absent; the Lite free-tier generated 285,000 signups since launch; search visits 6.2 million (up 3x in two years).

qa_highlights.question: Is the IB and M&A turnaround happening, and is software use by bankers a lead indicator?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IB and M&A are recovering and that some banking customers are expanding usage, but emphasised that the core investor segment is still flattish and it is not banking on a rebound.

qa_highlights.question: Is ASP falling as the business shifts?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended ASP fell from about Rs 5 lakh to about Rs 4 lakh per account per year, mainly from mix shift toward cheaper accounts; per-account pricing for like-for-like customers has held up.

qa_highlights.question: Has the TMX partnership produced revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Not yet; the TMX partnership is in pilot, with small revenue expected to grow. Larger enterprise partner deals take one to two quarters to close and launch.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company manage employee cost and profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is scaling thoughtfully, expects margins to expand non-linearly once revenue re-accelerates, and is not targeting a breakeven date; it did not commit to a specific margin timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company buy back shares given its valuation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it had a prior buyback and is becoming eligible for another; it favours using cash for growth investments, and buyback or dividend will be considered once accumulated losses are cleared.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Lite free tier convert to paid users, and can individuals sign up?
qa_highlights.answer: Lite is a major funnel for PLG; management did not disclose conversion rates. Sign-up requires an organisational email, and individual users can contact investor relations for access.

risks_watch: Deal volume at a 10-year low in venture funding; any slowdown in IB/M&A recovery would hit the core investor segment.
ASP erosion from mix shift toward lower-priced accounts; management said ASP is still at about Rs 4 lakh.
Sales-team doubling and FY27 product spend may keep EBITDA negative; watch the cost-to-revenue trajectory.

Q4 EBITDA was pressured by a step-up in advertising linked to the Bhujia and Kya Baat Hai Ji campaigns, plus a Bengal-election labour exodus and a 2.5-day factory shutdown. Management took a price rise of about 3% in April 2026 to offset edible oil and packaging inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H2 EBITDA margin fall to about 11% from about 13.5-14% in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to advertising, which was about 3.2-3.3% of sales in Q3/Q4 versus about 1% in H1, plus about 50 bps of one-time doubtful-debt provisions in the last two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the difference between consolidated growth of 19% and standalone growth of 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: The gap is mainly THF retail, worth about 2.2 percentage points of growth, with Bikaji USA and Ariba also contributing; management confirmed there is no inorganic contribution this year.

543654|2026-03.headline: Medanta FY26 total income rose 20% to INR 45,089 million and Q4 set a record, with Noida losses narrowing to INR 236 million in Q4.
543654|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA, with total income up 25% YoY to INR 11,958 million and PAT up 40% YoY to INR 1,417 million. Full-year PAT rose 15.1% to INR 5,541 million, while EBITDA including Noida was INR 10,560 million (24.2% margin). The newly inaugurated 550-bed Noida hospital ramped up, with its quarterly EBITDA loss narrowing from INR 320 million in Q3 to INR 236 million in Q4. Management guided to Noida breakeven in 2H FY27 and laid out a capex and bed-addition pipeline of roughly 2,700 beds over 3-4 years.

segments.name: International

qa_highlights.question: Can Noida reach breakeven by Q2 FY27 and what was its occupancy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects breakeven in 2H FY27, not a firm Q2 commitment. Current occupancy is around 30%; breakeven typically needs 40-45%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Noida's ramp-up structurally different from Lucknow and Patna?
qa_highlights.answer: Structurally no; the difference is that Lucknow and Patna opened during COVID. Noida is still missing pediatrics (started late FY27), obstetrics, and liver transplant.

qa_highlights.question: Gurugram demand and retention with new competitor hospitals coming in Sept-Oct?
qa_highlights.answer: No senior clinician lost so far. Management expects a war for talent and manpower cost pressure but is not worried on demand.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 and FY28 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR 800-900 crore; FY28 about INR 600-700 crore. Project-wise split not shared.

qa_highlights.question: Growth levers over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Adding services and specialties, bed additions across existing hospitals, about 10 OTs in existing hospitals, and minimally invasive and robotic work.

qa_highlights.question: Inorganic plans given strong net cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Several acquisition, partnership and O&M transactions under evaluation; no further deals disclosed beyond Indore.

543657|2026-03.headline: Archean Q4 FY26 EBITDA fell 34.3% YoY to INR66.4 crore on salt pricing and volume pressure, with the US-Iran conflict and Kutch logistics disruption driving the decline.
543657|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR304.7 crore, down 9% YoY, with reported EBITDA of INR66.4 crore (21.79% margin) and PAT of about INR29.8 crore. Industrial salt volumes fell 7.2% YoY to 1.1 million tons, with about 120,000 tons of customer deferrals and about 250,000 tons of shipments not completed due to logistics problems. Bromine volumes were about 3,731 tons, up 4% YoY, with realisation up 14% YoY and production back to historical daily rates since mid-February. Management said FY27 bromine growth targets remain 15-20% a year, with a longer-term goal of 40,000 tons, while Acume and Idealis Mudchemie ramp-ups have lagged expectations.

Bromine is back at about 55 tons/day, implying roughly 20,000-21,000 tons a year if sustained; the next milestone is 25,000 tons and then 40,000 tons over time.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited longer pharma product development cycles, pricing pressure as an entrant, and bromine supply constraints from Hajipir in Q2-Q3. Actions include a deeper sales team, new products (Zinc Bromide upgrade, PBR 3, two more alkali bromide products in H1 FY27) and process cost work.

On volume, it restated the 50-55 tons/day run-rate and a 15% higher FY27 target near 25,000 tons; the management team 'has expanded, not changed'.

qa_highlights.answer: Unsold finished salt inventory built up in Q4 because deferred orders and logistics constraints prevented shipments; captive bromine consumption figure was not provided and will be emailed.

qa_highlights.answer: No bromine price range given. rows.why: Onboarding yields ~22.5% with a further 10-15 bps compression expected, cost of funds down only ~15 bps and spreads guided flat, so NIM expansion from here is limited; credit cost relief is the main lever, with cost-to-assets flat at ~5.75-6% in FY27.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: FY27 (50-60 branches over the year, ~12 added in Q1)
rows.why: Branch network at ~856 after ~12 additions in Q1, with 50-60 more planned for FY27 as a run-rate of ~50-60 per year, so branch capacity keeps coming online through the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 disbursement guidance of INR 6,500-6,800 crore (Q1 run-rate plus ~10%) and AUM growth ~20% reiterated; June at ~INR 670 crore and a new normal of INR 600-650 crore per month, with AUM at INR 13,722 crore (+4% QoQ) only partly reflecting the pickup.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Credit cost trending toward 1.7% (low end of 1.7-1.9%) and disbursements at a record INR 1,496 crore, with June at ~INR 670 crore, could support upside if slippages fall as management expects.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Incremental borrowing cost guided at ~8.5% with spreads flat and no repo hikes assumed, while slippages at 0.70% flat QoQ must turn down in Sep, Dec and Mar quarters for the 1.7-1.9% credit cost guide to hold; rate hikes or ADB ECB hedging costs are the named risks.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: within ~3-6 months of the call (roughly Q2-Q3 FY27)
rows.why: Management plans one more product beyond micro LAP and housing within 3-6 months, with details to follow; housing launched about two quarters ago.

rows.label: Move to 2x D/E
rows.why: Management expects D/E of 2x in 6-8 quarters as net worth adds ~INR 1,100-1,200 crore PAT annually; net worth is INR 7,653 crore at 30 June, with ~INR 1,850 crore liquidity on balance sheet.

rows.label: Asset quality stabilisation
rows.why: Management expects slippages, credit cost and NPLs to trend down in these quarters; current book at 83.30% (vs 82.69% in Q4) to reach ~85% by end FY27, and 30+ DPD at 12.38% (vs 12.69%).

rows.label: No yield re-pricing up
rows.why: Management says higher collection costs will be recovered via lower credit cost, not higher lending rates; onboarding yields ~22.5% with 10-15 bps further compression expected.

tone.note: Management was confident on record disbursements, collections and the asset-quality direction, but cautious on borrowing costs, energy and rate risks, and deferred rollback, 60-90 DPD and collection-efficiency questions to the IR team; analysts pushed on yield compression, cost of borrowing, write-o

543663|2026-09.headline: Five-Star Q2 FY27: record disbursements of Rs 2,078 crore (+74% YoY) and PAT of Rs 299 crore, but management flags spread compression ahead.
543663|2026-09.overview: Disbursements hit a historical high of Rs 2,078 crore, up 39% QoQ and 74% YoY, while AUM reached Rs 14,640 crore (+14% YoY). Collection efficiency improved to 98.2% and 30+ DPD fell to 11.5% from 12.38%, though GNPA was sticky at 3.48%. PAT was Rs 299 crore, including a Rs 19 crore one-time tax benefit (about Rs 281 crore underlying). Management guided to tighter spreads as cost of funds rises, partly offset by a roughly 1% yield hike on incremental loans effective October 2026.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 299 crore (Rs 281 crore excluding Rs 19 crore one-time tax benefit)
about 7.5% in Q2; about 7.35-7.40% for the year

segments.name: Core geographies (Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana)
segments.commentary: Together more than 80% of AUM; management reports no drought-like stress and collections holding up. Tamil Nadu collects best, followed by Andhra and Telangana.

segments.name: Karnataka
segments.commentary: Management says collections are improving month-on-month after the state ordinance impact, and disbursements are being pushed more firmly there.

segments.name: Ticket-size mix (disbursements)
segments.commentary: Sub Rs 3 lakh about 26-27%, Rs 3-5 lakh about 51-52%, above Rs 5 lakh the balance. Target steady state is about 25/50/25.

guidance_outlook: Expect flattish credit slippages and credit cost for the rest of FY27; slippage around 70 bps for the next couple of quarters.
Incremental yields up about 1% from October 2026, but absorbing it across the book will take roughly 24-36 months (about 8 quarters per management on one question).
Incremental cost of borrowings expected 8.70-8.75% in H2 FY27; book cost of funds to exit FY27 about 12-15 bps higher, near 8.90%.
Spread compression expected: about 10-12 bps for H1 and about 10-15 bps by FY27 exit; margin expansion ruled out.
Growth guidance to be comfortably exceeded; any revised guidance likely after Q3. Opex to AUM to fall 50-75 bps over the next couple of years, to 6.75-7%.
October disbursements about Rs 550 crore (muted), with November and December expected to pick up.
capex_capacity: Added 19 branches in Q2 and 75 over the last year, focused on deepening presence in core geographies.
Active loans about 5.1 lakh, up 5% YoY.
Liquidity about Rs 1,300 crore at September 30; unavailed sanctions about Rs 1,100 crore.
Raised incremental debt of Rs 825 crore at an all-in cost of 8.43%; bank borrowings about 69% of total (67% in Q1).
Second tranche of ADB facility still pending, with hedging cost on the higher side.
demand_pricing: Customer rates raised about 1% on incremental disbursements across risk categories, from about 21-23% to about 22.5-23.9%, effective October 2026.
Top-up loans are about 10-15% of disbursements (Rs 200-300 crore per quarter); incremental top-up disbursal about 50% of the outstanding.
Management says yield hikes will not raise defaults, citing that loans above Rs 5 lakh earlier carried the same yield as sub-Rs 3 lakh loans.
Insurance commission impact from the IRDAI circular is nil, as Five-Star passes insurance premiums through without earning commission.
Gold loan overlap: 40-50% of customers have some gold loan; meaningful overlap about 30-40%.

qa_highlights.question: How will asset quality move given the rainfall deficit, and any stress signs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no drought stress in core states; collections in October are in line with July and September, with October D1C1 expected near 98%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the repayment rate rising, and what is the behavioural tenure?
qa_highlights.answer: Repayment rises due to adjusting outstanding on internal top-ups (about 1-2% extra repayments); behavioural tenure to move closer to 4 years, from the 36-37% repayment rate.

qa_highlights.question: How much have customer rates been raised, and when does yield bottom?
qa_highlights.answer: About 1% on incremental disbursements; management agreed that yields have bottomed this quarter, but margin expansion is not expected.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the write-off recovery trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Recoveries take about 18-24 months given no SARFAESI access on loans below Rs 20 lakh; H1 recoveries were about Rs 20 crore and NPA resolutions Rs 35 crore in Q2 (Rs 25 crore in Q1).

qa_highlights.question: How will cost of funds and spread move?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental cost of borrowing to rise 20-25 bps vs Q2, with book cost up 12-15 bps by FY27 exit; H1 spread hit about 10-12 bps, roughly 8 bps post-tax.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Legal expenses from the scaled-up legal recovery vertical and CSR spend based on the 3-year average profit.

risks_watch: Rate cycle: a further 25-50 bp repo hike would add to cost of funds beyond the 10-15 bps built in; December policy is a key watch point.
Stage-3 at 3.48%, with Stage-3 rising about 7-8% in absolute terms; management expects a trend-down only in a couple of quarters.
61-90 DPD bucket slippages flat, leaving a sticky stock in the bucket that drives the 70 bps slippage run-rate.
Written-off pool recovery slow (about Rs 300 crore written off in the last 8 quarters vs Rs 150 crore earlier); management has agreed to consider more disclosure.
MFI exposure about 35-40% of customers and no fresh scrub done; a sector relapse would test the collections set-up.
Revised guidance to come only after Q3; new product line still undisclosed, with details promised next quarter.
543663|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth, collections and operating momentum, with repeated use of phrases like 'historical best'. Cautious and specific on spreads, GNPA stickiness and recovery timing, and evasive on specific AUM growth targets.
key_quotes: Our upward trajectory in disbursements continued during the current quarter as well, where we recorded our historical best disbursement of Rs. 2,078 crores, up 39% over previous quarter and 74% year -on-year.
We expect flattish credit slippages and credit cost for the rest of the year, despite the industry headwinds.
No, margin expansion is not possible , Nischint, because we are already seeing the effect of the repo rate increase on our existing borrowings.
Our book is fixed. So, we will not be able to change the rate on the existing book. Fresh disbursements will come in at 1% higher yields.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Spread compression of 10-12 bps in H1 and 10-15 bps by FY27 exit as incremental cost of borrowing rises to 8.70-8.75% against a ~1% yield hike on incremental loans; management explicitly rules out margin expansion.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 19 branches added in Q2 and 75 over the last year, with continued deepening in core geographies; no quantified capacity plan beyond branch rollout, so call is likely rather than surely.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Disbursements hit Rs 2,078 crore (+74% YoY) and AUM is up 14% YoY to Rs 14,640 crore, though October disbursements are muted at about Rs 550 crore with a pick-up expected in November and December.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: AUM growth guided to comfortably cross earlier guidance, with any revised guidance possibly after Q3; record Rs 2,078 crore disbursements (+74% YoY) back this up.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management expects flattish credit cost and slippage around 70 bps, and says AUM growth will comfortably exceed earlier guidance; the risk is spread compression of 10-15 bps by FY27 exit rather than a guidance cut.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: A new product line is undisclosed, with details promised next quarter; no size or timing beyond that.

rows.label: 1% yield hike on incremental loans from October 2026
rows.why: Customer rates raised about 1% on incremental disbursements (from about 21-23% to 22.5-23.9%), but absorbing it across the book will take roughly 24-36 months, so it only partly offsets cost-of-funds rise.

rows.label: Rate-cycle risk to cost of funds
rows.why: A further 25-50 bp repo hike would add to cost of funds beyond the 10-15 bps already built in; book cost of funds exits FY27 near 8.90% versus 8.78% now.

rows.label: Opex to AUM decline
rows.when: over the next couple of years
rows.why: Opex to AUM guided to fall 50-75 bps to 6.75-7% from about 7.35-7.40% for FY27, though Q2 ran at about 7.5%.

tone.note: Management was confident on record disbursements, collections and growth, and cautious and specific on spread compression, sticky GNPA and slow recoveries; analysts probed the rate cycle, asset quality stress and yield timing.

543664|2026-03.headline: Kaynes FY26 revenue rose 33.2% to INR3,626 crore, but missed the INR4,500 crore then INR4,000 crore guidance, with operating cash flow of about INR600 crore negative.
543664|2026-03.overview: Management attributed the revenue shortfall to West Asia-related customer deferments, supply chain delays and one large EV two-wheeler customer cutting volumes by about 90%. Consolidated FY26 EBITDA was INR5,741 million (15.8% margin) and PAT INR3,639 million (10% margin), with Q4 revenue of INR12,426 million (+26% YoY) and PAT of INR912 million. Cash flow weakened sharply, driven by the smart metering subsidiary (Iskraemeco) with receivables of about INR1,365 crore, while the standalone EMS business turned cash positive. Management declined to give a specific FY27 revenue number and instead guided to outgrowing the market at roughly twice the market growth rate.

financial_highlights.change: PBT hit by about INR32 crore of quarterly intangible amortisation
from 83 days FY24; management also cited 64 to 54 days

segments.name: EMS (standalone/KEMPL)
segments.commentary: FY26 EMS revenue about INR2,655 crore (Q1 INR442 crore, Q2 INR683 crore, Q3 INR667 crore, Q4 INR862 crore), growing about 26-30%. Standalone EMS operating cash flow INR250 crore positive versus INR65 crore last year; EMS receivables INR399 crore at year end versus INR379 crore at start.

segments.name: Smart metering (Iskraemeco subsidiary)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR971 crore (roughly 24-25% of group revenue), with receivables about INR1,365 crore, of which about INR250 crore non-current. Installation delays in rural areas and state-government/DISCOM payment cycles are holding up collections; securitisation has discounted only about INR40 crore so far.

segments.name: OSAT
segments.commentary: Unit 1 fully operational; Unit 2 to commercialise by Q2 FY27. Management cites revenue visibility above INR25,000 million over five years. Sanand facility inaugurated by the Prime Minister; FY27 production estimate INR250-300 crore, export-oriented.

segments.name: PCB
segments.commentary: Management sees a confirmed demand pipeline for five years with customers seeking more capacity. FY27 production estimate INR300-400 crore; first year of operation.

segments.name: Rail (Kavach)
segments.commentary: Kavach has initial approval and trial orders; approvals expected in H1 FY27, with bulk orders in H2. Management expects rail revenue to grow about 20-25% with margins above 30%.

segments.name: EV / automotive
segments.commentary: EV segment grew about 28% in FY26 despite the large two-wheeler customer falling about 90%. Company is moving from PCB supply into assemblies and products.

guidance_outlook: No explicit FY27 revenue number; management guides to growing at about twice the market rate (market cited at 15-18% EMS growth), with quarterly updates on market versus Kaynes growth.
Standalone EMS to stay cash positive, with working capital days improving by about 8-10 days in the coming years.
Consolidated operating cash flow: management expects the INR600 crore negative to fall by 70-80% by Q3 FY27 and turn positive by year end.
Metering receivables and installation expected to be completed within about 3 quarters; the business will move to an EMS-component-only model for new orders.
Target of NPD-led and value-added revenue at nearly 30% of total revenue over the coming years.
Smart meter FY27 revenue expected roughly flat to slightly up or down versus INR971 crore, with about 50% of volume on the old model and about 50% on the new model.
Quarterly amortisation of acquired intangibles (Iskraemeco and August Electronics, about INR320 crore) going forward, after the Q4 catch-up of about INR32 crore.
capex_capacity: OSAT Unit 1 fully operational; Unit 2 to commercialise by Q2 FY27 (Sanand facility inaugurated by the Prime Minister).
FY26 intangibles rose to INR536 crore from INR238 crore, mainly from acquisitions of Iskraemeco and August Electronics (Canada, North America EMS), with about INR320 crore capitalised.
Mysore facility crossed INR10,000 million revenue in FY26.
Metering: about 35 lakh meters on current order, plus a possible 3.5-4 lakh-meter extension; 2-3 months needed to complete pending supply, with installation taking 1-2 quarters more.
Launched three products now in production (SOP started), and a 9-month product launch cycle versus 12-18 months previously.
Investing in NPD engineering, co-development, digital and R&D infrastructure, and predictive maintenance / Industry 4.0 at 2 plants.
demand_pricing: Order book above INR9,000 crore, described as diversified and non-cancellable; management says there is no structural deterioration in demand.
Q4 and FY26 shortfall attributed to West Asia conflict, last-minute customer deferments, supply chain delays and product timing shifts; some revenue recognition shifted though orders remain valid.
Auto industry outlook cut from mid-double-digit growth (December projection) to single-digit or low double-digit, per management, which raised caution on offtake.
Aerospace, railway, defence, space and EV are being added to reduce dependence on any one vertical.
OSAT and PCB output expected to be export-oriented at first; internal versus external consumption still being decided.

qa_highlights.question: Viral Shah: What is the sanctity of guidance given the INR4,500 crore then INR4,000 crore targets versus about INR3,600 crore actual, and the OCF miss?
qa_highlights.answer: Management apologised, said the INR4,500 crore target implied about 55% growth, and blamed a large EV two-wheeler customer dropping about 90% of volume plus government project delays. On OCF, it said standalone EMS was cash positive at INR250 crore while the metering business drove the consolidated outflow.

qa_highlights.question: Nitin Arora: Why no guidance, and what will move the INR600 crore negative OCF to breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it now commits to outgrowing the market at twice market growth rather than a number. It expects the INR600 crore negative to fall 70-80% by Q3 FY27 and turn positive by year end, with metering installations the key lever.

qa_highlights.question: Renu Baid Pugalia: Share of metering in revenue, growth ex-metering, rail ramp-up and government-offtake risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Metering is about 20-25% of revenue, but about 60% of that business was already EMS supply. EV grew about 28%. Kavach has initial approval and trial orders, with H1 approvals and H2 bulk orders expected; rail growth of 20-25% is targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Amber Singhania: Metering subsidiary revenue, EBITDA and receivables; why receivables rose despite the securitisation plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Metering revenue was INR971 crore and receivables about INR1,365 crore. Securitisation has only started with one bank, with about INR40 crore discounted in each of two quarters, because the bank needs first-month billing and collections; installation delays are the main constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Dhaval Somaiya: Pending meter count, and breakup of the other roughly INR740 crore of subsidiary revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Pending supply to be completed in 2-3 months, with a possible 3.5-4 lakh-meter extension. Of the EMS revenue of INR2,655 crore, two foreign entities contributed about INR300 crore on average, and KEMPL is the main EMS subsidiary.

qa_highlights.question: Sumant Kumar: Why did intangibles rise by about INR300 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisitions of Iskraemeco and August Electronics capitalised about INR320 crore of intangibles. Amortisation was booked once in Q4 (about INR32 crore), and will now be booked quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: Achal Lohade: Do the INR1,000 crore OSAT and INR500 crore PCB production targets still stand?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh Kunhikannan said no such guidance was given. He estimated FY27 PCB output at INR300-400 crore and OSAT at INR250-300 crore, both export-led.

risks_watch: Receivables and cash flow: metering receivables of about INR1,365 crore, of which about INR250 crore non-current; securitisation has discounted only about INR80 crore cumulatively.
Guidance credibility: the company missed its INR4,500 crore then INR4,000 crore revenue targets, and the CFO was unavailable for the call due to health reasons.
Top management restructuring and role realignment flagged during the quarter.
Customer concentration: a large EV two-wheeler customer fell about 90%.
Government payment and installation dependency for smart metering; DISCOM and GENCO timelines.
Quarterly amortisation of acquired intangibles now recurs (about INR32 crore per quarter), which will depress PAT.
Auto industry outlook downgraded; OSAT and PCB ramp and internal versus external sales mix still undecided.
543664|2026-03.management_tone: Defensive and apologetic on the guidance miss and cash flow, while confident on the EMS business, OSAT and PCB growth. Management was evasive on specific FY27 revenue and cash targets, offering market-relative growth and quarterly updates instead.
key_quotes: We did an aggressive top line growth in the year based on the order book and we got the electrification of the vehicle.
As I said, it is not a denied order, it is a delayed order. We sincerely apologize for that this has happened.
We are committing for our growth based on what market can pull in.
Our order book continues to be stronger at INR9,000 crores plus.
I think the inflection point has stopped and will come into the reduction, and we will come back in 3 quarters with positive results on specifically this entity.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 FY26 operational EBITDA margin was 15.6% and FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin 15.8%, but quarterly intangible amortisation of about INR32 crore now recurs and metering mix is lower-margin, so margin gains are conditional on OSAT/PCB ramp and NPD mix reaching the targeted ~30% of revenue.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2 FY27 for OSAT Unit 2; PCB first year in FY27
rows.why: OSAT Unit 2 is set to commercialise by Q2 FY27 and FY27 production estimates are INR250-300 crore OSAT and INR300-400 crore PCB, with a INR9,000 crore+ order book and OSAT revenue visibility above INR2,500 crore over five years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management commits to growing at about 2x the EMS market (15-18% market growth implies roughly 30-36%), EV grew 28% in FY26 despite a ~90% drop at one customer, and FY26 EMS revenue grew about 26-30% to INR2,655 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed directly; FY26 intangibles rose to INR536 crore from INR238 crore mainly through acquisitions, and utilisation was not disclosed, so a fresh capex announcement is conditional on OSAT/PCB ramp and cash flow recovering.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Company missed INR4,500 crore then INR4,000 crore revenue guidance with FY26 at INR3,626 crore, has no numeric FY27 target, and the CFO was absent from the call, so an upgrade is unlikely to be offered soon.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Operating cash flow was about INR600 crore negative against marginally negative guidance, metering receivables are about INR1,365 crore with only about INR80 crore securitised, and auto outlook was cut to single-digit or low double-digit growth.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Three products are already in production (SOP started), the product launch cycle has shortened to 9 months from 12-18, and NPD-led revenue targets nearly 30% of total revenue; Kavach rail approvals expected in H1 FY27 with bulk orders in H2.

rows.label: Metering receivables collection and securitisation
rows.why: Management expects the INR600 crore negative OCF to fall 70-80% by Q3 FY27 and turn positive by year end, with metering installations and collections as the key lever; metering receivables are about INR1,365 crore.

rows.label: Standalone EMS working capital days improvement
rows.why: Standalone EMS working capital days fell to 53 from 83 in FY24 and standalone EMS was cash positive at INR250 crore versus INR65 crore last year.

rows.label: Kavach rail bulk orders
rows.when: H1 FY27 approvals, H2 FY27 bulk orders
rows.why: Kavach has initial approval and trial orders; management expects rail revenue to grow about 20-25% with margins above 30%.

tone.note: Management was apologetic and evasive on the missed INR4,500 crore then INR4,000 crore guidance and the negative OCF, while confident on EMS, OSAT, PCB and rail; analysts pressed on guidance sanctity, metering receivables, securitisation and intangible amortisation.

543664|2026-06.headline: Kaynes Q1 FY27 revenue rose 40% to INR946 crore and EBITDA rose 31% to INR147.6 crore, but operating cash flow was negative INR259 crore as inventory and metering receivables rose.
543664|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 40% YoY to INR946 crore, driven by EMS (standalone EMS up 53%, overseas up 327% on the August Electronics acquisition), while smart metering fell 12% YoY to about INR204 crore as management deliberately curbed supplies over collections. EBITDA was INR147.6 crore at a 15.6% margin, with management flagging margin pressure from component and PCB cost inflation and lead times of 6 to 8 months. Negative operating cash flow was about INR259 crore (management also cited INR235 crore in another bridge), with inventory up about INR177 crore and receivables up about INR68 crore. OSAT and PCB commissioning remains guided for Q3 FY27, with a FY27 revenue target of INR450 to 500 crore across both.

segments.name: EMS (overall, incl. overseas)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR854 crore including GST, with 40% overall EMS growth and about 48% growth cited by management; collections of INR847 crore. Receivables in EMS were about INR613 crore at quarter end versus INR606 crore at the start.

segments.name: Smart metering (GridCrest)
segments.commentary: Sales about INR240 crore including GST against collections of INR88 crore, so production and supply were halted. Metering receivables rose from INR1,158 crore to INR1,311 crore; about INR200 crore was received in early July.

segments.name: OSAT (Kaynes Semicon)
segments.commentary: Capex to date about INR700 crore; government subsidy of INR170 crore received till July 2026. Commercial billing expected from Q3 FY27; Unit 2 on track for operation by Q3 FY27. Mitsui partnership for Japan access announced.

segments.name: PCB (Kaynes Circuit)
segments.commentary: Capex to date about INR500 crore, with about INR250 crore in transit. Commercial production to start next quarter; one global customer has requested the entire capacity and trials are ongoing with a vendor code approved.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth committed at 2x the market growth; no absolute top-line number given. Market grew about 17% in Q1.
OSAT and PCB combined FY27 revenue target INR450 to 500 crore, with revenue starting from Q3 FY27.
FY27 capex plan: about INR300 crore OSAT, about INR300 crore PCB and about INR250 crore EMS; Q1 spend about INR230 crore in total across these.
Management expects profitability to take a couple of quarters to normalise; FY27 described as a difficult, tough year.
Management expects receivables turnaround in the metering business and cash-positive position by end of FY27.
Working capital to be reported on a rolling 12-month basis going forward.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR180 crore (per management in the call), against a broader plan of about INR300 crore each for OSAT and PCB and about INR250 crore for EMS.
Capex in FY26 was INR473 crore for OSAT and INR324 crore for PCB.
Kaynes Semicon Unit 2 and Kaynes Circuit Chennai remain on track to be operational by Q3 FY27, despite minor slippage from West Asia-related equipment and logistics disruption.
Government subsidy of INR170 crore received in OSAT till July 2026, with more subsidies expected to fund further capex.

First 3U satellite in prototype; launch targeted mid-next year pending regulatory testing and an ISRO launch date (PSLV or GSLV). Titanium gas bottle manufacturing via Crio Precision and Aerotech for ISRO and DRDO.
demand_pricing: Order book of more than INR8,900 crore; management said Q1 order additions exceeded deliveries.

New logos include a second-largest Indian two-wheeler EV maker (serial supply begun after about 8 months of development), German and French global brands, and a leading Indian wireless operator; management cited about 72 customer visits in the quarter.
Component prices up about 30% to 35% per management; PCB prices up about 3x; lead times more than 6 to 8 months in some categories; PCB suppliers demanding advance payment.
FX impact on imports about 3.3% of import level, per management.
Pass-through to customers is on a quarter-on-quarter basis and may lag; management said agreements with strategic customers allow some price pass-through.
Aerospace recovered in the quarter; management said growth was seen across railways, automotive, aerospace and defence.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EMS growth excluding metering, and what is the EBITDA bridge and metering strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said overall EMS grew 40% and metering 28% (per one answer), with standalone EMS up 53% and metering down 12%. Lower other income after QIP proceeds (about 2.5 points on PBT/PAT) and higher depreciation were cited for margin pressure. Management said it is exploring models to divest the service portion of metering to keep receivables off the balance sheet, with details promised by February.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cash flow from operations and metering revenue for the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said operating cash flow was negative about INR259 crore (inventory up INR177 crore and receivables up INR68 crore), versus negative INR379 crore in Q1 FY26. Another bridge given later cited INR235 crore; the company's cash profit was about INR158 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are the receivables, inventory and payables figures?
qa_highlights.answer: Total receivables (current and non-current) rose from about INR1,765 crore to INR1,925 crore. Inventory days were about 105 at Q1 end versus 96 earlier. Management said the 12-month rolling receivable days were about 163 and the quarterly figure about 190.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 revenue growth and the OSAT/PCB FY27 and FY28 scale-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management committed to 2x market growth without an absolute number, citing market volatility. OSAT and PCB together are targeted at INR450 to 500 crore of FY27 revenue from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How much of component cost inflation is captured and will gross margins compress?

qa_highlights.question: What are the EBO/SIS capex and FOCO economics?

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold as more stores are added and the mix shifts?

qa_highlights.question: Could growth exceed 35% and can the company fund growth without new equity?

qa_highlights.question: How do gold and silver price spikes affect margins?

qa_highlights.question: Why were store additions accelerated to 32 in FY26?

543711|2026-03.headline: Sula Q4 FY26 revenue rose 7% YoY to INR 142 crore, but gross margin pressure from grape mix kept EBITDA roughly flat in absolute terms.
543711|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue returned to growth at 7% YoY to INR 142 crore, driven by a 5% rise in Own Brands and 17% growth in Wine Tourism revenue. Gross profit fell 3% YoY as a shift to wine grapes and higher wine carryover cut gross margin by about 350-400 bps, and the absence of a prior-year INR 3.5 crore Karnataka inventory gain added about 150 bps of pressure. Management cut operating costs 3% YoY, holding EBITDA at similar absolute levels, and PAT fell 34% on a high prior-year tax credit. Full-year FY26 revenue fell 2% to INR 596 crore excluding a prior-year one-off, with Own Brands down 5%.

qa_highlights.question: How do channel inventory levels and discounting in the market compare with recent years?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel inventory came down somewhat at end-Q4 after Q3 destocking. Sula runs far lower discounts than domestic peers, while industry discounting is unsustainably high and some producers may fail.

qa_highlights.question: Will Sula import wines and distribute them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is looking at it but will proceed cautiously, saying Own Brands offer better profitability than imports and that importing has low barriers to entry and is hard.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be more acquisitions in Wine Tourism?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it is always open to opportunities and keeps looking, but the Chandon deal needs further investment and no others are yet agreed.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost pressures and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: COGS rose in Q4 on grape mix, which will persist for a couple of quarters until the next harvest. Overhead reductions are expected to offset part of this at EBITDA level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the resort plan for FY27 and the elite/premium strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific resort launch announced; a plan to be disclosed by next call. Elite and premium share reached 79% in Q4, and management is not guiding for further gains.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to 30%, and what is the FY27 top-line outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not guide to a return to 30% margins soon, expects moderation, and sees growth as the driver of any margin expansion. It is cautiously optimistic about YoY margin improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Can receivables be monetised, and are there plans for other liquor categories or a Chandon resort?
qa_highlights.answer: Telangana corporation payments have resumed after the new excise policy, and receivables are seen as under control. Management is focused on Wine Tourism; no non-wine spirits deal has been found, and the Chandon resort timing and room count were not given.

qa_highlights.question: Where does Wine Tourism's revenue mix and key target stand?
qa_highlights.answer: Wine Tourism is about 19% of FY26 revenue and may rise 200-300 bps in FY27. Keys are to grow in high double digits over two years, with a next project above 200 keys in about 1.5 years.

543711|2026-06.headline: Sula Q1 FY27 revenue rose 3% to INR121 crore, but gross profit fell 5% as wine-grape mix and adverse market mix cut margins by ~350 bps.
543711|2026-06.overview: Net revenue from operations grew 3% YoY to INR121 crore (INR118 crore in Q1 FY26), the sixth consecutive month of positive sales growth per management. Elite & Premium grew 6% and Own Brands grew 2%, while Economy & Popular stayed under pressure from competitor discounting. Gross profit fell 5% on a ~150 bps hit from a shift to wine grapes (near 100% of harvest 2026 procurement vs 80% earlier) and a ~200 bps hit from adverse geographic mix. Management says the grape-cost headwind should ease from Q4 FY27 and fully normalise from Q1 FY28, and expects EBITDA margins to recover to last year's levels before FY27 end.

qa_highlights.question: Has competition behaved rationally on raw material costs, given the company's 50%+ share of the mass segment, and what is the past behaviour of other players?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cannot guarantee it, but says wine production volumes have been flat to declining as players found the business unsustainable, and table grape prices are expected to fall well below harvest 2026 levels after a more-than-doubling versus prior harvests.

qa_highlights.question: Has the wine industry been flat over the last 3-4 years, and are there plans to diversify into faster-growing categories such as white spirits?
qa_highlights.answer: Wine saw little growth in the last two years per IWSR, with only low single-digit industry growth; excise data is hard to obtain in some states. Management is hopeful the destocking cycle has bottomed, has no white spirits plans now, but has new segments in the pipeline to be detailed later.

qa_highlights.question: Had the grape mix stayed the same, would gross margin have been better or worse, and what is the upside from the mix shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin would have been better, since raw material costs would not have risen as they did. Management said it is too early to quantify any upside, but the negative impact will not be present from Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for table grape prices and how far has the blend moved from the strategic mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Table grapes were typically procured at under INR15-16/kg and spiked to about INR35/kg in harvest 2026; prices are expected to fall below INR20/kg. Some sub-INR600 wines now carry 60-70% wine grapes versus the intended almost exclusively table-grape blend.

qa_highlights.question: Do Maharashtra's MML policy or Karnataka's excise changes benefit Sula, and why is Karnataka still weak?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said MML is spirits-only and wine duties are unchanged in both states, so no benefit. Karnataka's weakness is category-wide degrowth in Q1 and H2 FY26; Sula held or gained share in Elite & Premium but lost share in Economy & Popular. Hot June and delayed monsoon shifted some consumption to beer.

qa_highlights.answer: No separate asset base is reported for Wine Tourism; management says its EBITDA margin is better than standalone wine. 543720|2026-06.headline: KFin Q1 FY27 revenue grew 30% YoY to consolidate Ascent (ex-Ascent ~10%), while PAT was flat-to-down and EBITDA margin fell to 34.2% with Ascent.
543720|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose 30% YoY, with about 9.6% growth excluding Ascent, and 2.7% QoQ including Ascent (1.6% excluding). EBITDA grew about 7.1% YoY, but consolidated EBITDA margin was 34.2% with Ascent versus 39.4% without it. PAT margin was 21% including Ascent and 26.6% excluding it, and PAT was broadly flat to marginally down YoY. Management raised its FY27 growth outlook to EBITDA growth of 17-20% and PAT growth of 12-15%, while a yield decline of about 2% QoQ in mutual funds was attributed to debt-to-liquid mix shift and provisioning for a pending large-client renewal.

financial_highlights.change: About INR 200 crore to go to dividend already declared

financial_highlights.value: About 51% of EBITDA converted to free cash flow

financial_highlights.change: from US$5.7 million in Q4; US$4.4 million in Q1 FY26 (pre-consolidation), +32% YoY

segments.name: Domestic mutual fund (RTA/fund admin)
segments.commentary: Industry AUM grew about 15% YoY versus KFin about 16%; KFin's equity AUM market share rose about 80 bps QoQ. Yield fell about 2% QoQ, of which about 30% was debt-to-liquid mix and the rest mainly provisioning for a pending large-client renewal.

segments.name: Issuer solutions
segments.commentary: Managed about 80% of main-board IPO issue size in Q1 and holds about 50% of NSE 500 market share (versus ~52% earlier). Corporate actions are about 30% of issuer revenue; the company guided to tepid corporate actions in Q2 due to IT services dividend deferrals.

segments.name: International (Ascent and global fund solutions)
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 200% YoY with Ascent and about 32% organically. Ascent EBITDA margin was about 8%; management targets double-digit margin within 12 months. Sequential decline ex-Ascent was attributed to pipeline timing, with growth expected above 25%.

segments.name: Alternatives (XAlt, GIFT City)
segments.commentary: About 731 funds with about 37.3% market share, targeting close to 40% with pending launches. 15 new AIF wins in Q1; the AIF business has compounded above 60% over four years and management expects at least 40% growth going forward.

segments.name: Pensions (NPS)
segments.commentary: Reached break-even last quarter and now contributes about 15%+ EBITDA margin. Manages about 2.5 million pensioners and is the second-largest CRA in India.

segments.name: Wealth management (mPower Wealth) and technology
segments.commentary: Three wealth platform mandates won. An INR 25 crore+ big-data mandate runs over about 18 months, with INR 40 crore of signed bolt-on deals across 3-15 month durations.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR guided at 18-20%, unchanged from prior guidance.
Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 40-45%; management aims to hold 40% threshold including Ascent by end of FY27.
FY27 visibility of EBITDA growth of about 17-20% and PAT growth of 12-15%, ahead of the earlier high-single to low-double-digit indication.
Ascent to become EBITDA accretive by end-FY27 or early FY28; double-digit margin targeted within the next 12 months; KFin-level EBITDA margin expansion to take three to five years.
Cost optimisation benefits expected from Q2 FY27 onwards; mutual fund yield expected to stabilise, with management unwilling to guide a yield number.
Target of at least 20% of revenue from controllable (non-market) businesses; currently about 6% from VAS plus 5-6% from other non-market businesses.
capex_capacity: Ascent cost base is being rationalised through shared support functions, consolidated office space and better vendor contracts (AWS, Oracle, Microsoft); contract renewals roll into KFin structures in October and January.

Mutual fund platform transformation under FinEx: SIP processing now completes within three working days for 99.7% of transactions (versus about 21 days industry); next launch by end-calendar 2026 to automate non-commercial and purchase transactions.
Cayman Islands facility being set up to meet regulatory substance requirements, a near-term cost already in the plan.
Infrastructure cost pressure (servers, routers, laptops) noted; management will be harder on client discount negotiations.
demand_pricing: Mutual fund yield fell about 2% QoQ: debt-to-liquid shift (debt yields 2-2.5x liquid) contributed about 30% of the decline, and provisioning for a large-contract renewal this year accounted for the rest. Management guides against a fixed yield number, citing asset-mix and AMC-growth effects.
Ascent revenue hit by digital-asset fund markdowns, offset by six new fund managers with over US$100 million each (transitions taking 3-5 months) and fund launches.

Retail participation is still weak, with Demat net additions slowing despite IPOs; IPO pipeline includes PhonePe, Zepto, Jio, Manipal Health and Razorpay, plus Razorpay, Garuda and Pushp Brand mandates won.
Management expects strong corporate actions outside IT services; IT services firms have deferred dividends, which could weigh on Q2.
Pending Philippines government contract: KFin is reported as highest bidder on technical and commercial scores, but no award has been announced.

qa_highlights.question: Karthik (Indus Capital): What cost takeouts drove better domestic MF segment margins despite single-digit revenue growth and yield compression, and can segment margins bottom out if yields stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited technology-led cost optimisation across payroll, non-payroll and licensing, not ad-hoc cuts; full increments were given this year. It said yield is driven by pricing/discounts, asset mix and AMC growth, and that pricing-driven stability is expected from here, with the SIP automation and next FinEx launch (by end calendar 2026) as controllable margin levers.

qa_highlights.question: Karthik: how much of the PAT gap (about INR 47 million between INR 799 million and INR 752 million) narrows via cost takeouts versus revenue growth, and over what period?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is both, weighted more to top-line growth at Ascent (EBITDA about 7-8%), while KFin-level cost optimisation will do the heavy lifting. PAT pressure is largely non-cash amortisation of goodwill/contract payments and capitalised One Constellation platform costs.

qa_highlights.question: Swarnab Mukherjee (360 ONE): Is the yield drop only debt-to-liquid mix, how should yield be modelled over the remaining three quarters given ~2% QoQ fall, and how will bolt-on wins add revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said equity mix was stable and the shift was debt to liquid (debt yields 2-2.5x liquid), plus provisioning for a large renewal this year. It declined to guide a yield number, saying conservatism means sticking to about 3% annual decline, though a reversal could give an upside surprise. Bolt-on deals of about INR 40 crore signed in Q1 run for 3, 6 and 15 months and are episodic, not annuity.

qa_highlights.question: Swarnab: why did international ex-Ascent revenue fall QoQ, and how should it be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Mathur said the decline reflects contracts in the pipeline that will materialise in coming quarters, not a fundamental change. He expects growth above 25% and called it a one-quarter phenomenon.

qa_highlights.question: Arjun Bagga (DSP MF): what is the split of the yield decline between debt-to-liquid mix and renegotiation provisions, and will Ascent margins reach double digits next quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30% of the 2% yield decline came from debt-to-liquid; the remaining ~1.7% was net of asset-class moves, mainly provisioning for pending renegotiation, partly offset by ETF-to-equity movement. Double-digit Ascent margin is targeted within the next 12 months, not next quarter; the QoQ fall reflected crypto fund markdowns offset by new wins and fund launches. On discounts, management said it will be harder on client discount negotiations given infrastructure cost pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijeet (Kotak): number of Ascent $100m+ clients, whether the wins are new or transitions, Ascent AUM vs revenue mix, deal size and FY guidance.
qa_highlights.answer: Six new fund managers with over $100 million each were won; these are transitions from incumbents, taking 3-5 months. The INR 25 crore data mandate is a single client with two contracts over about 18 months, milestone-based. Management gave FY27 visibility of EBITDA growth of 17-20% and PAT growth of 12-15%, ahead of the earlier high-single to low-double-digit indication. It did not give a digital-asset revenue split.

qa_highlights.question: Madhukar (JP Morgan): Ascent dollar revenue QoQ and yield, and Southeast Asia (GFS) yield.
qa_highlights.answer: Ascent revenue rose from US$5.7 million in Q4 to US$5.9 million, +32% YoY against US$4.4 million in Q1 FY26 pre-consolidation. Vivek said the Southeast Asia margin improved on AUM growth there and hoped it would be sustained, without confirming the 5.3 bps yield.

qa_highlights.question: Prayesh Jain (Motilal Oswal): Philippines contract timing and profitability, issuer-solutions growth versus company growth, segment profitability, and wealth management economics.
qa_highlights.answer: No Philippines win has been announced; KFin is reported as highest bidder on technical and commercial scores, and the client has not awarded the contract. Corporate actions are about 30% of issuer revenue, and retail participation remains weak. Wealth pricing has two models: fixed platform-implementation fees (20-35% of contract value) and basis points on AUM. Segment profitability was referred to IR.

risks_watch: Mutual fund yield: about 2% QoQ fall in Q1 with about 1.7% left after the debt-to-liquid effect; further renegotiation provisions for a large renewal this year; no yield number guided.
Corporate actions in issuer solutions (about 30% of issuer revenue) guided tepid for Q2 as top-tier IT services firms defer dividends; retail participation and Demat net additions are slowing.
Ascent margins: about 8% EBITDA, with double-digit targeted within 12 months; crypto fund markdowns weigh on AUM and revenue; consolidated margin is 34.2% including Ascent versus 39.4% without.
Cost-optimisation benefits are guided from Q2 FY27, and the PAT gap is driven by non-cash amortisation and capitalised platform costs. Watch for PAT growth converting to the guided 12-15%.

Philippines government contract remains unawarded; bolt-on tech deal revenue (about INR 40 crore signed) is lumpy and phased over 3-15 months; the Cayman Islands substance facility adds near-term cost.

So, we have moved a couple of notches from there. And whilst, as you know, we do not necessarily give formal guidance, we have visibility for EBITDA growth closer to 20 %, anywhere between 17% to 20%, and our PAT numbers anywhere between 12% to 15%.

543720|2026-09.headline: KFin Q2 FY27: consolidated revenue up 30% QoQ including Ascent (10% ex-Ascent); EBITDA margin 40% incl. Ascent, 45.8% ex-Ascent; FY27 guidance held.

Consolidated EBITDA margin was 40% including Ascent and 45.8% excluding it, and PAT crossed Rs. 100 crore (up 33% YoY, 7.5% QoQ per the call). Management said FY27 estimates are unchanged despite a recent market correction, citing buffers from discretionary spend deferrals. Ascent (Middle East exposure about 25% of its revenue) remained a drag on margins and client additions were flat.

segments.commentary: About 13% of revenue; value-added services (7.5% of total revenue) spiked in Q2 on AGM/e-voting and corporate actions. Management guides about 20% YoY growth for the year, with Jio Platforms IPO handled as RTA.

segments.commentary: Revenue growing 30%+ in each operating geography; EBITDA margin about 8% this quarter vs 7-7.5% last quarter and about minus 12% a year earlier. Management targets double-digit margin in the next couple of quarters and about 20% next fiscal year.

segments.commentary: About 7% of revenue. Pensions grew 42% YoY vs industry 12-13% and broke even about three quarters ago; management said margins for these businesses are transitional due to ongoing transition costs.

Issuer solutions expected to grow about 20% YoY for the year, with upside to 20%+ if large IPOs such as Jio Platforms come through.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sequential MF yield stabilisation and will it hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yields rose about 2% QoQ on pricing discipline, AMC mix and asset mix; it expects yields to stay largely consistent based on visibility into late October.

qa_highlights.question: Can issuer solutions strength continue through the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided about 20% YoY issuer solutions growth, with corporate actions concentrated in Q2 and some spillover into Q3; IPO revenue is under 2% of issuer solutions revenue annually.

qa_highlights.question: What are the buffers if capital markets worsen?
qa_highlights.answer: Discretionary transformation, IT, automation, geographic expansion and product launch spend can be deferred if financials weaken, with some budgeted spend over the next five months at risk of deferral.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Ascent employee cost keep rising and when will its margin ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Ascent's EBITDA margin was about 8% vs 7-7.5% last quarter; it targets double digits in a few quarters and about 20% next fiscal year, with KFin-level margins in two more years. Standalone Ascent EBITDA is positive and cash breakeven gap is about Rs. 3.5-4 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the tax rate rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Loss-making new entities (KFin services, GIFT City, Thailand) have no deferred tax recognised, and Ascent's Singapore losses prevent foreign tax credit, so the rate is above 25.64% for KFin India; GIFT City migration timing is not guided.

qa_highlights.question: Why were Ascent client additions flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fund managers delayed launches amid market conditions; 80-90 contracted funds are awaiting launch in the coming weeks, and H2 is seasonally stronger for Ascent.

543732|2026-03.headline: Radiant CMS standalone revenue flat in FY26 at INR1.69 trillion cash handled; consolidated PAT fell to INR280 million from INR470 million on fintech losses.
543732|2026-03.overview: Standalone revenue was flat YoY in FY26, with cash handled up about 1% to INR1.69 trillion, as railways region losses and an e-commerce client loss offset growth. Standalone Q4 EBITDA margin was 15%, up from 13.6% (some sources cite 30.6% for Q3, which conflicts with the 13.6% cited by the CFO). Consolidated PAT dropped to INR280 million from INR470 million, mainly from losses at fintech subsidiary Radiant Acemoney after the PIDF subsidy ended in December 2025. Management set targets of breakeven for RVL and Acemoney in H1 FY27 and consolidated EBITDA of 15%+, while the buyback was described as under consideration.

segments.name: Core retail cash management (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue flat in FY26 after losing railways regions (about INR9-10 crore annualised) and an e-commerce logistics client (about INR4 crore annualised). Service points reached 77,521, with 2,173 added in Q4 and 118 new clients and 230 new customers added during the year. E-commerce grew 21%; petroleum and organised retail also grew well.

segments.name: Radiant Valuable Logistics (RVL)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR60.7 million in FY26 with a loss of about INR60 million. Management expects breakeven in H1 FY27 and says 25-30% of lanes have turned profitable; it added five marquee jewellery chains and targets 20% steady-state EBITDA margin rising to 30%.

segments.name: Radiant Acemoney (fintech subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR287.8 million in FY26 (+19.6%), with about 1.5 lakh POS merchants onboarded and about 60,000 soundboxes added. Q4 was weak after the PIDF subsidy ended on 31 December 2025; Q4 standalone subsidiary revenue was a little under INR1 crore. Over 10,000 business correspondents are now live, and management targets H1 FY27 breakeven.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for consolidated revenue of INR5 billion and PAT margin of 11-12% in FY27, with mid-teens longer-term PAT growth; no formal guidance was issued.
Core business revenue growth target of 12-14% (mid-teens per Q&A) in FY27 is needed for PAT of about INR60 crore.
Consolidated EBITDA immediate target of about 15%+ and breakeven for both RVL and Acemoney in H1 FY27.
Acemoney breakeven needs roughly INR4.5 crore quarterly revenue, per the Q&A discussion of the analyst's estimate.
Management expects positive impact from bank discussions on fuel-cost pass-through (cash logistics association approached banks) from H1 FY27; no outcome yet.
Direct customers are about 18% of revenue, with a target of around 30% within two years.
capex_capacity: Service points 77,521 at year end; 2,173 added in Q4 FY26 but total points slightly down YoY due to railways losses. Management says the point-addition plan is unchanged.
Dedicated cash van contract rolling out; two to three more large contracts in pipeline. Cash-on-operations is about 12% of revenue.
Acemoney has 1.5 lakh+ POS machines and about 60,000 soundboxes, with plans for more deployments via small finance banks and NBFCs.
Radiant is applying for a payment aggregator licence at the holding-company level with the RBI.
demand_pricing: Railways and e-commerce losses weighed on core revenue; management is pursuing direct clients, dedicated cash vans, and smaller and cooperative/rural banks.
A large project order from an existing customer began rollout from 1 April 2026; an analyst estimated it adds 3-4% to the top line.
Cash logistics association has approached banks on fuel-cost charges; management expects a favourable outcome to be possible from H1 FY27.

Acemoney sells through tripartite arrangements with small finance banks and payment aggregators, with one-time rollout fees plus transaction revenue. Management says transaction revenue carries no material cost.
Management said that 37 banks offer retail cash management services but only two nationwide providers exist, which it cited as a competitive advantage.

qa_highlights.question: What is the direct-customer share of revenue and where will it go?
qa_highlights.answer: Direct customers are about 18% of revenue, up from about 1% earlier and about 13% last quarter; management says 30% is a reasonable target within two years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company considering a buyback given its cash and valuation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a buyback is being explored with larger shareholders and advisers, with no decision yet; it also highlighted its dividend record.

qa_highlights.question: What were the FY26 losses at RVL and Acemoney?

segments.commentary: Installed capacity 55,000 MT per annum; four plants on 14 acres covering about 75% of wagon and coach body manufacturing. Capacity added via two new sheds (6,000 and 11,000 sq ft) and cutting and slitting lines, with capex of over INR30 crore in the year.

segments.name: NS Engineering Projects (NSEPL, 74% owned)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 65,000 MT, up from about 12,500 MT when acquired. Produced 56,380 MT in FY26; galvanizing bath running at about 24,000 MT per year, with a plan to scale to about 85,000 MT in the same space.

segments.name: Cosmic Springs and Engineers (CSEL, wholly owned)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 13,600 MT, produced about 7,300 MT per management. Springs output about 2,300 MT at near-zero margin pending RDSO licence; forging unit targeted for commercial production within about nine months.

segments.name: Amzen Transportation (pending acquisition)
segments.commentary: Wagon capacity 3,600 per annum, targeted to rise to 7,200 with capex; also bridge girders up to 20,000 MT per RDSO approval. Management estimates the total project cost at about INR400-odd crore and plans sea freight containers at about 7,500 to 10,000 units.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume guidance: installed capacity of roughly 122,000 to 130,000 MT, with output at 88-89% utilisation; management said the company should reach about 175,000 MT in 12-15 months.
Management said FY27 top line should be at least about 30% higher than FY26, with a 20-25% upside if the infrastructure and railway cycle holds.
Target of about 350,000 MT by FY29 across all units including Amzen; at about INR100,000 per tonne, management indicated about INR3,500 crore revenue.
Springs margin expected to rise to about 10% and then 15-18% PAT after RDSO licence, which management expects by next month.

Amzen timeline: LOI by June, then 90 days of approvals and repairs, with first commercial production targeted within about nine to twelve months; expected Amzen capex of about INR200 crore funded by debt.
Management said the company will apply for main board migration in early July 2026 once eligibility is met, and said raw material prices could rise 7-10% in H2 FY27.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 133,600 MT as of date; actual production about 106,370 MT in FY26 versus 55,000-56,000 MT last year.
Forging unit under construction, with commercial production targeted in about nine months.
NSEPL galvanizing expansion on newly acquired adjacent land, adding about 20,000 MT of installed capacity.
RDSO licence for springs is pending after about 75% of testing is done; management expects approval next month.
Amzen capex to lift wagon capacity from 3,600 to 7,200 per annum over about two years.
demand_pricing: Order book of INR760 crore covering infra and railway items, up from INR500-550 crore last year.
Management expects raw material prices to rise 7-10% in H2 FY27, with long-term contracts and price variation clauses used to pass through costs.
Raw material pricing moved from about INR52,000-53,000 per tonne last year to about INR60,000 this year, per management.
Management cited a possible railway procurement of 1 lakh wagons (about INR40,000 crore TAM) and an industry capacity of about 40,000-45,000 wagons per year.
West Bengal government infrastructure expansion (metro, bridges, cofferdams, sheet piles, crash barriers) cited as a potential order source; no specific orders named.

qa_highlights.question: What are the revenue and volumes for springs and forgings in FY26, and what are the margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Springs volume about 2,300 MT and total fabrication plus steel about 4,500 MT. Springs revenue INR67 crore but profit only about INR1.5 crore because RDSO licence is pending and sales go to traders, not railways. Forging has not started.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT margin dilute in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three reasons: weak springs profitability, about INR2-2.5 crore carrying cost of Amzen KMPs, and about INR10 crore legal and related costs on Amzen, which auditors did not allow to be capitalised. Total hit about INR8 crore to PAT.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Amzen award final, and could anyone bid again?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Supreme Court set aside the NCLAT order, restoring the H1 bidder status it held when the NCLAT order came; the CoC must now scrap the new Form G and resolution plans and negotiate with the company.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt position and funding plan for Amzen?
qa_highlights.answer: Term loan about INR36 crore plus working capital of INR84 crore from SBI and Bank of India; cash of about INR150 crore. Amzen is expected to need about INR200 crore of debt, with peak debt of about INR300 crore term and INR300 crore working capital by FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline from LOI to Amzen production?
qa_highlights.answer: LOI expected by June, then 60-90 days of repairs and AMCs, with first commercial production targeted by March-May 2027 and at most about a year.

qa_highlights.question: Is 100% growth guidance still intact for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth of no less than 100% is the promoter's aspiration but could not be assured because raw material prices and government spending are outside its control; it framed FY27 at 30% or more.

qa_highlights.question: How will raw material price volatility be managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Stock levels, price variation clauses on railway contracts, traders for smaller purchases, and future hedging once volumes reach about 200,000 MT, plus liquid metal initiative for diversification.

qa_highlights.question: Would the NSEPL 26% minority buyout be pursued?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it wants to consolidate the 26% minority holding in NSEPL via a SEBI-route process, with a merchant banker report and shareholder approval, and said it is for consolidation only.

risks_watch: Amzen LOI and CoC approval are still pending; timing depends on procedural steps and possible further legal challenge, and the company's legal costs have already weighed on FY26 profit.
Springs business has near-zero margin until the RDSO licence is granted; a delay would continue to weigh on consolidated margins.
Raw material price volatility (steel, wheel sets) with management guiding for a 7-10% increase in H2 FY27 and limited contract pass-through on existing orders.

543929|2026-03.headline: HMA Agro FY26 standalone revenue rose 39.2% to INR 67,689 million, with EBITDA up 80.3% to INR 2,109.5 million.
543929|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as the company's strongest year, with standalone revenue of INR 67,689 million (up 39.2% YoY) and standalone PAT of about INR 1,271 million. Q4 FY26 standalone revenue was INR 15,384.83 million, up about 4% YoY from INR 14,368.2 million. Consolidated revenue was INR 69,164.95 million (up 34.7%) with consolidated EBITDA of INR 2,839.59 million and margin of about 4.11%. The Q&A was short and several answers were deferred to email, including geography split, Philippines target, and rice revenue.

Pipeline initiatives mentioned at an early stage: frozen French fries and chicken, with no volumes or timelines disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Geographic split of FY26 revenue across top five geographies?
qa_highlights.answer: Not provided on the call; management will email a continent-wise breakdown.

qa_highlights.question: Was the 25% Philippines sales target for FY26 achieved?

qa_highlights.question: How do the company's buffalo meat prices compare with local peers in Vietnam, Malaysia and the Philippines?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said local domestic prices there are higher due to limited livestock and import dependence; it gave no percentage discount and will follow up by email.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Middle East situation affecting operations and what drives input cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight and shipping costs have risen many-fold and could pressure pricing if unresolved. Input costs depend on demand-supply, weather, transport and farmer pricing; the company cannot fully pass these on.

qa_highlights.question: Update on the rice business and FY26 contribution; is INR 1 billion FY27 revenue on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Rice has repeat orders and a growing client base but the FY26 figure was not disclosed. Management reiterated the INR 1 billion FY27 target and said it aims to reach it soon.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for product portfolio expansion, and the pricing basis for the OFS?
qa_highlights.answer: Early-stage plans include frozen French fries and chicken, with no numbers. The OFS floor price was set by the board on current market value to achieve minimum public shareholding via a stock exchange window; management said SEBI rules allow the seller to set the price.

risks_watch: Freight and logistics cost escalation from Middle East conflict could squeeze margins if customers cannot absorb higher prices.

Quarterly EBITDA was INR431 million (11.7% margin) and PAT was INR224 million (6.1%), both the highest margins of FY26 on a sequential basis. For FY26, revenue fell 17% to INR12,615 million, normalized EBITDA was INR1,302 million (10.3%), and reported PAT rose 7.7% to INR733 million. qa_highlights.question: Will the bank keep growing microfinance, and what is the risk weight on incremental MFI loans?

543952|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 25% YoY to INR5,651 million, but organic constant-currency growth was only 5% after excluding the North American real estate contract.
543952|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached INR5,651 million, up 25% YoY, helped by MST and SweetRush acquisitions; constant-currency growth was 11.4% YoY and 2.9% QoQ. Ex-acquisitions growth was 11% YoY, and organic constant-currency growth was 5% after normalising for the North American real estate (RECO) contract that ended in FY26. EBITDA was INR1,032 million (18.3% margin), up 8.5% YoY, and PAT was INR574 million, up 16.4% YoY. Management kept FY27 guidance of high single-digit revenue growth and an 18–20% EBITDA margin, and guided Q2 to 9–11% YoY growth with margins around 18%.
