qa_highlights.question: When will AI-enabled learning investments meaningfully contribute to revenue, and has the FY27 EBITDA margin guidance changed?
qa_highlights.answer: AI-enabled services were 13% of Q1 FY27 revenue and are expected to grow as a share over time. FY27 EBITDA margin guidance remains 18% to 20%, unchanged from last quarter; Q1 margin was 18.3%.

qa_highlights.question: What is organic YoY growth excluding RECO, and what would QoQ organic growth look like?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic constant-currency YoY growth ex-RECO is 5%. Overall CC growth normalised for RECO is about 18%. QoQ growth of about 2.9% is overall and was not affected by RECO, since RECO was absent in both quarters; management said MST and SweetRush were in both quarters so the QoQ figure is roughly 3% on a like-for-like basis.

qa_highlights.question: Including RECO, what is organic YoY growth? Why is there no slowdown QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RECO contributed about 6% to last year's numbers, and including it, organic YoY growth would be about negative 1.7%. Management described RECO as a contract that ended in FY26 as a result of Ontario deregulating that education, not a lost client.

qa_highlights.question: What were the margins ex-SweetRush and when will the 20% long-term margin be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give ex-SweetRush margin. It reiterated the 18% to 20% range for FY27 and said margins should get back to close to 20% at overall level as the business scales.

qa_highlights.question: What drives high single-digit full-year growth given 3% QoQ, and is there Q2 slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 QoQ growth will dampen due to the European summer vacation quarter, revive in Q3 and flatten in Q4. Some wins could accelerate growth but management will talk about them only once more certain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation plan given net cash and free cash flow: buybacks, acquisitions, or higher dividends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is actively looking at acquisitions and significant AI infrastructure investment will absorb capital. Three acquisitions were done since the capital kitty was created, more are in the pipeline, and it is keeping a consistent dividend policy; no buyback was announced.

qa_highlights.question: Why was revenue visibility up only slightly QoQ despite three annuity wins, and what drove the Top-5 client share rising from 31% to 35%?
qa_highlights.answer: Visibility is net of revenue consumed and new order intake; it grew 19% YoY to USD462 million. The three wins were average-sized, not large (large is over $5 million). The rise in Top-5 share was from a large client added in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin profile of AI revenue and is there a subscription element?
qa_highlights.answer: AI revenue margins are better than the company average. Management described post-training coaching and simulation subscriptions lasting 6 to 12 months, similar to SaaS, with one client of about 12,000 users renewing after the first year.

qa_highlights.question: Why were MST and SweetRush prior-year numbers not shared?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said last year's numbers for the acquired entities are unaudited and were prepared under different revenue recognition models, so it would not discuss them.

543953|2026-03.headline: FY26 EBITDA rose 95.69% to INR126.99 crores at a 6.19% margin on total income of INR2,051.02 crores (+15.71%).
543953|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 total income of INR2,051.02 crores, up 15.71% YoY, with EBITDA of INR126.99 crores (+95.69%) and PAT of INR89.42 crores (+98.87%). H2 FY26 total income was INR1,098.26 crores (+8.1%), with EBITDA of INR73.21 crores (+102.79%) and PAT of INR50.72 crores (+103.6%). Management attributed margin gains to a shift toward higher-margin designer, diamond (Vajraa Diamonds) and retail products, and a new Chennai flagship showroom opened about two months before the call. Management reiterated 25-30% growth guidance and, in one answer, cited 35% PAT growth for FY27. The call was heavy on generalities, and several answers on inventory, KPIs and the gold-policy impact lacked hard data.

segments.commentary: Serves over 1,000 clients per management, with more than 500 B2B clients served every year; management says 80-90% are repeat clients and no client exceeds 5% of volume. Ticket size not quantified.

segments.name: B2C (retail)
segments.commentary: Retail share of sales is about 10% today, with a target of 25% within about two years; retail margins cited at 10-12%. Chennai flagship has 10,000 sq ft total area and about 6,800 sq ft sales area, opened about two months before the call, with a INR450-500 crore revenue target.

segments.name: Vajraa Diamonds (diamond jewellery)
segments.commentary: Management says the premium diamond brand is gaining traction and has added to margins; no figures were disclosed.

Retail target of INR450-500 crores for the new store in the near future.
Retail share of sales to rise from about 10% to at least 25% within the next two financial years.
No fundraising planned; expansion to be funded internally.

Plans to open smaller-format stores initially in Tamil Nadu, later pan-India; location search under way, no count or capex disclosed.
Manufacturing is asset-light, using artisan units spread across India; no owned capacity or utilisation data given.
demand_pricing: Management said there is no slowdown in demand despite high gold prices; any dip lasts about 1-2 months.
Management described the government's request that citizens stop buying gold for a year as a short-term impact, expecting exchange and recycling of household gold to add business.
Management said no margin decline is expected from the gold-buying appeal and that gold price falls of 15-20% would have little impact on margins.

Working capital: management gave overall working capital cycle of 52 days and inventory cycle of 70-75 days, with the increase attributed to retail stocking. These figures were not reconciled in the call.
Management did not give a split of FY27 growth between gold price and volume.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins hold at current levels over the medium term if gold prices stay flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shift to designer and higher-margin items supports sustained margins and expects further improvement, without quantifying it.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the inventory cycle is 70-75 days and overall working capital cycle is 52 days, with receivables collected within about a week at most; the payable figure was not given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the average ticket size in wholesale and retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Wholesale ticket size is not defined because it varies by client; retail average invoice size is INR1.5-1.7 lakhs.

qa_highlights.question: Is the gold-buying appeal affecting margins or top line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no margin decline and any top-line effect would be short-lived.

qa_highlights.question: What is the projected sales for the new flagship?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave a target of INR450-500 crores in the near future; it said sales per sq ft cannot yet be measured after two months.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 growth and PAT expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 25-30% growth and said it is confident of 35% PAT growth in FY27 due to higher retail margins.

risks_watch: Retail ramp-up: inventory days rose with stocking for the new store, and management gave a 70-75 day inventory cycle against a 52-day overall working capital cycle; the INR450-500 crore store target has not yet been tested.
Government gold-buying appeal and possible duty changes could dampen discretionary demand; management expects only a short-term effect.
Inventory of about INR400-408 crores is large relative to the scale of the business; watch whether inventory grows faster than sales.
Retail share target of 25% depends on store execution and is still to be delivered.
Guidance of 35% PAT growth for FY27 is above the stated 25-30% revenue target; watch for clarification.
Management gave little detail on KPIs, payables, cash flow, debt or capex, which limits the analysis.

543953|2026-06.headline: Khazanchi Q1 FY27 revenue rose 45% YoY to INR586.36 crore and PAT 84% to INR27.83 crore, with EBITDA margin at 6.82%.
543953|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 45% YoY to INR586.36 crore, EBITDA rose 89% to INR39.98 crore and PAT rose 84% to INR27.83 crore, with margins expanding 158 bps (EBITDA) and 99 bps (PAT). Management attributed the quarter to the first full quarter of the new flagship showroom and ERP rollout. The company is migrating from BSE SME to the main boards of BSE and NSE, which management expects to complete in about 2 months, and it reiterated a INR5,000 crore revenue target by FY30 with 25-30% growth and B2C reaching ~40% of revenue. Several answers were vague (volume split, store capex, quantum sold), and the call ran on a mix of expansion plans and operating metrics.

qa_highlights.answer: Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin is about 16.4%. About 25-27% of stores are COCO. Accessories expansion is framed as raising wallet share and SSSG, building on belts, wallets and caps.

qa_highlights.question: Payable days appear to have dropped sharply; what is driving this?
qa_highlights.answer: Management initially deferred the question and the CFO said he would revert, citing payable days history of about 171-188 days in recent years.

risks_watch: Inventory at about 170 days versus the 150-day target; operating cash flow and short-term borrowings depend on this.
Payable days reportedly fell sharply (about 55 days per an analyst's reading); management has not yet explained this.
Raw material cost pressure; price increases are deferred until after September, and no price hikes are taken.
Gross margin optics shaped by e-commerce rebate accounting; EBITDA margin band is wide (16-19%).

543957|2026-06.headline: Redtape Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 19.4% YoY to INR47 crore on 3.7% revenue growth to INR480 crore, with no price hikes and e-commerce deliberately de-prioritised.
543957|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 3.7% YoY to INR480 crore, with gross margin at 47.5% and EBITDA margin at 20.4%. PAT rose 19.4% to INR47 crore, the company's highest-ever Q1 profit in absolute terms. Management held MRPs flat and absorbed minimum wage and input cost inflation through sourcing, supply chain and retail efficiencies. E-commerce declined as management refused to match marketplace deep discounting, and online share of revenue fell to 22% from 30%. Management described the e-commerce dip as a one-off, but gave no quantified guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Analyst cited >200 bps improvement; management attributed it to retail margins, operating leverage and supply chain
down from around INR28 crore in Q1 FY26, due to lower e-commerce platform rebates

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: 56% of Q1 turnover; management says footwear carries Q1 and Q2 while apparel peaks in Q3 and Q4. Open footwear ASPs improved sequentially.

segments.name: Apparel
segments.commentary: 39% of Q1 turnover; seasonally stronger in Q3 and Q4. Category-wise YoY growth not disclosed.

segments.name: Accessories
segments.commentary: 5% of Q1 turnover. Sunglasses are in about 80% of stores; hard luggage in only 10-15% of stores as the category has shifted online.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Declined YoY because management declined incremental marketplace discounting. Online share fell to 22% from 30%. Management aspires to return to 30%.

segments.name: Core India retail
segments.commentary: Softer early in the quarter, improved as the quarter progressed. Management credits store-led model and better product/category mix for margin gains.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: UAE franchise stores were hit early in the quarter and recovered in the last month. UK master distributor Style Label Manchester appointed; transactions started. No export revenue guidance given.

segments.name: Sprandi (new brand)
segments.commentary: Sports brand acquired in April 2026 for India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka and other countries. Shoes first, then apparel. Launch in India online and retail by end-September 2026.

guidance_outlook: Store additions: 33 opened in Q1 FY27; aspiration of about 150 (150-plus) by FY27 end, versus an earlier 200-250 aspiration. Management says it will 'remain close to that number'.
EBITDA margin to be kept stable at around 20% for the year; management also expressed aspiration to increase margins.
Revenue growth: management hopes to continue the growth rate of the last 3-4 years; no quantified FY27 guidance.
E-commerce share expected to recover towards 30% of revenue; management called the Q1 dip a one-off.
Inventory target to reduce from 173 days to 150 days. Inventory build-up expected in Q2 ahead of festive season.
No MRP increases planned; management aims to offset cost inflation through efficiencies.
capex_capacity: New stores: 33 opened in Q1 FY27, with an aspiration of about 150 for FY27. Ramp-up takes 45-50 days for a 1,000 sq ft store and about 75 days for a 3,000-4,000 sq ft store.
New store formats are mostly 800-1,500 sq ft, as expansion into South, East and West India is more store-count intensive.
Store in Forum Mall, Kolkata opened; malls to be used where they are stronger than high streets, particularly in South and West India.
Inventory at 173 days; Q2 build-up expected, then reduction in Q3 and Q4.
No acquisitions in the pipeline at present; management is open to opportunities in footwear and apparel.
demand_pricing: Demand was soft early in Q1 due to macro headwinds and cautious consumer spending, then improved through the quarter.

Marketplaces pushed higher discounting; Redtape declined to match beyond levels it considered appropriate for the brand. Management said there is no fixed discount ceiling and that it decides event by event (for example BBD).

ASPs rose sequentially across footwear and apparel from product and category mix, not broad-based price hikes. MRPs were held flat despite minimum wage and input cost inflation linked to the ongoing war.
Management declined to quantify inflation, calling it 'a regular business'.
Non-BIS inventory remains; the industry has an extension of one year, with management expecting a further extension.
A September 2025 income tax search is ongoing; management says no material claim or risk has been identified so far.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the e-commerce weakness, and what is the discount level beyond which Redtape will not participate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline was a deliberate choice, not a structural weakness. It declined to set a fixed discount threshold, saying it depends on event size and margin impact, and that it expects e-commerce to recover.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inflation burden and will price hikes follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said minimum wage and war-related costs were absorbed, MRPs were not raised, and it would not quantify the inflation as it is a regular business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the lower other income?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Vivek Agnihotri said lower e-commerce platform rebates cut other income to around INR8-9 crore from about INR28 crore in the prior-year quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin improvement above 200 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said retail margins were stronger, with operating leverage and an optimised supply chain. No category-level margin split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Does Q1 margin mean moderation is likely for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the intent is to keep margins intact and aspire to improve them, while noting that it will not sacrifice margins for top-line growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the income tax search from September 2025?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the process is ongoing and could take 2-3 years, with no material claim or risk identified to date.

risks_watch: E-commerce recovery to 30% of revenue is an aspiration; online share is 22% and management gave no timeline or quantified discount threshold, and the Q1 dip could persist into the BBD/festive season if marketplace discounting stays deep.

Margin stability: management aims to hold EBITDA margin around 20% and gross margin gains (>200 bps per analyst) were attributed mainly to retail margins without a category-level split, so sustainability is unverified.

Inflation exposure: minimum wage hikes in manufacturing states and war-linked input costs were absorbed without MRP increases; no quantification given, so a squeeze on margins if efficiencies fade is a watch item.
Store rollout: 33 stores opened in Q1 versus a FY27 aspiration of about 150-plus (earlier 200-250); new 800-1,500 sq ft formats in South, East and West India may ramp more slowly.
Inventory at 173 days with a Q2 build-up planned ahead of festive season; reduction to 150 days targeted, and non-BIS inventory remains outstanding.

Income tax search (September 2025) ongoing; management said it could take 2-3 years, with no material claim identified so far. Other income fell to INR8-9 crore from about INR28 crore on lower e-commerce rebates.
key_quotes: So we don't see this as a weakness. The degrowth in e-commerce was largely a conscious outcome of our channel strategy during the quarter.
We would like to believe it's a one-off thing.
Not really. It's a regular business for us.
We would like to remain as it is now. We'd like to be stable.
But as of now there's been no claim of any material and there's no risk of any material.

543959|2026-03.headline: SBFC Q4 FY26: AUM up 29% YoY to INR 11,270 crore, PAT up 30% to INR 123 crore, credit cost steady at 1.38%.
543959|2026-03.overview: SBFC reported Q4 FY26 AUM of INR 11,270 crore, up 29% YoY and 8% QoQ, with gold loans reaching 21% of the book. Spreads widened 56 bps YoY to 9.09% as cost of borrowing fell 83 bps to 8.52%, and opex fell 69 bps YoY to 3.93%. PAT rose 30% YoY to INR 123 crore, with FY26 PAT at INR 451 crore (+31%). Management kept FY27 guidance broadly unchanged: 5-7% quarterly growth, flat spreads, opex down 20-25 bps and credit cost range-bound around 1.38%. Branch count reached 251 with a plan to stabilise near 275.

financial_highlights.metric: Return on average AUM / average tangible equity

segments.name: MSME loans
segments.commentary: AUM INR 8,873 crore, 79% of book, with Q4 disbursements of INR 785 crore. Average ticket size remains below INR 2.5 lakh and LTV is about 56-57%.

segments.name: Loan against gold
segments.commentary: AUM INR 2,374 crore, 21% of book, growing 63% YoY; management says growth is mainly price-driven and the share may move toward 25%. Around 220 of 251 branches are pure gold branches.

segments.name: Co-origination (with ICICI)
segments.commentary: Co-origination was 16% of Q4 disbursements and 18-19% of AUM, and is expected to hold similar levels through FY27.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance unchanged at 5-7% per quarter; management says the segment could double the book in 3-3.5 years.
Spreads expected to hold at around 9% current level; over 90% of the book is variable-rate.
Opex expected to fall 20-25 bps through FY27 as new branches mature.
Credit cost expected to stay range-bound around 1.38%, with possible benefit of about 5 bps.
Branch network to stabilise at about 275 (from 251) during the year; 46 branches were added in FY26 against 25 guided.
Portfolio mix between MSME and gold expected at 75:25; co-origination at 18-19% of AUM.
Capital: at 33% CRAR, growth could run about 2 years before needing fresh capital, with CRAR falling to about 24-26%.

Currently present in about one-fourth of districts in operating states (about 30% per Aseem Dhru) across 15 states.
Management says it will not add DSAs or connectors for at least two years; direct model retained.
Leverage at 1.9x debt/equity; management says capital is sufficient for roughly two years of growth.
demand_pricing: Management said growth in gold has been mostly price-driven rather than tonnage-driven; gold prices are expected to stay range-bound or flat.
Disbursements have been soft YoY; management said it paused momentum in some South, East and West pockets, and could return to around INR 300 crore per month when conditions improve.
South disbursals and AUM grew more slowly last year, which lifted the West's share of AUM (management said mix to stay similar for two quarters).
Early April data showed no new stress in sectors hit by LPG and fertilizer pressures; bounce rates marginally lower.
Management expects no increase in cost of borrowing in FY27; G-Sec volatility and a temporary liquidity squeeze were flagged.

qa_highlights.question: Why is employee and branch opex per unit flat for many quarters, and how long can that continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Dayani said upfront investment in state, regional and supervisor layers is already in place, so incremental cost is mainly front-end staff at low unit cost; opex is still guided down 20-25 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Will SBFC need DSAs or connectors to sustain growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanket Agrawal said the current distribution can deliver about 20% disbursal growth next year, with no need for indirect channels for at least two years.

qa_highlights.question: Sensitivity of growth and gold mix to gold prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Dayani said gold growth is mostly price-driven; FY27 gold growth is pencilled in on full-year benefit from branches added in FY26, not on higher prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is credit cost guidance conservative given early delinquency improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Dayani said guidance is cautious given the macro (fuel, rainfall, heat); April numbers show no stress in LPG- and fertiliser-linked sectors.

qa_highlights.question: Path to ROE of 18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanket Agrawal said ROE is an outcome of ROA and leverage (about 4.57% ROA, 3.17x leverage, ~14.5% ROE); management called 18% optimistic and cited more than 15% ROE on 25% growth if ROA compresses about 25 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ARC sell-down a driver of reported GNPA?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanket Agrawal said ARC sales are used to clean up hard-to-collect assets and recoveries under SARFAESI; benefits flow to P&L. No extra provision overlay was held beyond the March model refresh.

risks_watch: Macro shocks: oil price pass-through, weaker rupee, poor monsoon/El Nino, Gulf remittance risk, all flagged by management.
Gold price reversal would slow the gold book, which is 21% of AUM and the main driver of growth.
Credit cost guided flat at 1.38% while stage 2 rose from about 6% to 16% (per Mahesh Dayani); watch slippage and 1+ DPD (benchmarked 7-9%).
Disbursement volumes are down YoY and branches added in gold and MSME may not reach productivity targets as planned.
Rating upgrade is possible but not guided; management declined to comment.

543959|2026-06.headline: SBFC Q1 FY27: PAT rose 29% YoY to INR 130 crores and spreads widened 39 bps QoQ to 9.48%, while 0+ DPD rose 70 bps and AUM grew 6% QoQ.
543959|2026-06.overview: AUM reached INR 11,922 crores (up 27% YoY, 6% QoQ), with MSME AUM at INR 9,271 crores and gold loan AUM at INR 2,631 crores. Spreads improved to 9.48% and NIM to 10.6%, helped by a 90 bps YoY drop in cost of borrowing to 8.42%. Management cited headwinds: lower gold-loan eligibility after April 1, 2026 rules, a regulatory cap on bank collateral for sub-20 lakh MSME tickets that hit co-origination, and softer login-to-disbursal conversion (34% vs 42%). Asset quality weakened QoQ, with 0+ DPD up 70 bps and GNPA at 2.66%, but Stage 2 ECL was raised to 16% from 6% and total provisioning reached 1.91% of assets.

financial_highlights.change: up by similar bps as spread (QoQ)
Stage 2 ECL raised to 16% from 6%; about 2x regulatory minimum

segments.name: MSME / small-ticket LAP
segments.commentary: MSME AUM INR 9,271 crores (+4.5% QoQ) and disbursements INR 809 crores (+3% QoQ). Co-origination, about 20% of disbursals and book, reset to about 10% after RBI collateral rule for sub-20 lakh MSME tickets; management expects a return to usual run rate from this quarter.

segments.name: Gold loan
segments.commentary: AUM INR 2,631 crores (+11% QoQ). Gold yields rose in the quarter and were the main driver of the 29 bps QoQ yield increase; management expects gold yields to stay range-bound, with at most a marginal decline.

guidance_outlook: Opex to average AUM to fall 25 bps in FY27 (reiterated), and to be closer to 4% or below by year-end as new branches mature.
Credit cost expected at 1.4%-1.5% for at least the next two quarters; Q1 was 1.45%.
Yield expected to stabilise in the 17.50%-17.75% range; spreads to be held above 9%.
Cost of borrowing expected to stabilise at current levels after upfronting borrowings and liquidity build-up.
Branch expansion limited to 10-15 in FY27, after 5 branches added in Q1 (total 256), with further expansion tied to returns from recent branches.
Management says guidance for the coming quarter is unchanged; AUM target path to INR 15,000 crores with higher liquidity held on balance sheet.
capex_capacity: Branch count 256 as of June 2026 after adding five in Q1; roughly 52 branches opened over the last year, with the bulk in H2 FY26.
Plan for FY27 is 10-15 new branches, with expansion gated on profitability of recently opened branches.
Closing liquidity INR 1,864 crores; management intends to hold higher liquidity as it grows toward INR 15,000 crores AUM.
Capital adequacy ratio 32%; tangible net worth INR 3,613 crores.
demand_pricing: Login-to-disbursal conversion fell to 34% from 42%; management expects it to hold near 35% as higher logins and co-origination recover.
Around 1,400 applications per quarter (about 7% of roughly 21,000 logins), or about INR 140 crores of disbursals, were not passing filters; management will not push loans that fail screens.
Sub-10 lakh household segment showing leveraged stress; CIBIL scores above 700 for about 90% of the portfolio, but eligibility is the binding constraint.
Competitors pricing aggressively or offering larger loan amounts; management chose to walk away from some business to protect spreads.
Gold-loan eligibility norms reset from April 1, 2026, and falling gold prices reduced the loan amount reaching customers.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the sub-10 lakh segment in its credit cycle, and how does that affect FY27 growth and profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said conditions there have not improved and it is watchful. Aseem Dhru cited household DSR near 14% per CLSA, and said the company does not know whether it is early or mid-cycle.

qa_highlights.question: Will SBFC add new products in the next 12-18 months beyond small-ticket LAP and gold loans?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it will focus on getting better at the existing two products and sees no need for new products or geographies to meet FY27 guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Increments were rolled out, and about 20-25 branches opened in Q4 FY26 plus 5 in Q1 brought their full-year staff costs into this quarter. Cost to AUM should fall as those branches mature over the next nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Was the 30 bps yield increase driven by higher risk-taking?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanket Agrawal said gold yields rose this quarter, adding to the yield improvement. Company yield is expected to stabilise at 17.50%-17.75%, with spreads held above 9%.

qa_highlights.question: Is credit cost stable at about 1.4% for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management expects credit cost of 1.4%-1.5% for at least the next two quarters; Q1 was 1.45%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for incremental yield and gold yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental yield is in the same 17.50%-17.75% range, slightly up because of gold. Gold yields are expected to be range-bound with at most a marginal fall; the recent 25-30 bps rise should not be extrapolated.

risks_watch: Sub-10 lakh household segment: management says conditions have not improved, CLSA household DSR near 14%, and the company cannot tell whether the cycle is early or mid; watch the disbursal mix and ticket size there.
Asset quality: 0+ DPD rose 70 bps QoQ and management called it homework for the current quarter, expecting stabilisation this quarter and rollbacks in later quarters; GNPA 2.66%.
Co-origination recovery: management expects co-origination to return to its usual run rate this quarter after the RBI collateral rule cut its share to about 10%; verify in Q2 disbursals.
Cost to AUM: opex 4.29% needs to fall to about 4% or below by year-end as branches opened in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 mature; employee cost stays elevated in the near term.
Funding and rates: management flagged an upward bias in Indian interest rates from crude above $100 and deposit rates, while saying cost of borrowing should now stabilise at current levels.
Gold yields: management says the 25-30 bps rise should not be extrapolated and gold yields may drift marginally lower; spread floor of 9% depends on holding yields at 17.50%-17.75%.
key_quotes: We'd rather over-insulate the P&L now than explain a surprise later, call it prudence with a margin of safety.
So, we don't want to, at this stage look at anything different or new.

543959|2026-09.headline: SBFC Q2 FY27 PAT rose 27% YoY to INR 139 crore, with ROE at 15.04% and AUM up 27% YoY to INR 12,592 crore.

Credit cost eased to 1.37% from 1.44% and Opex fell to 4.07%, while spreads widened to 9.63%. Management said the gold-loan delinquency rise after the RBI circular was the main source of higher Stage 2 assets, and that the MSME book has stabilised rather than improved. Management kept its 5-7% quarterly AUM growth guidance and warned against treating 9.6% spreads as a new norm.

segments.name: Gold loans

Capital sufficient to an AUM of about INR 20,000 crore before the next capital raise; ROE expansion expected as leverage rises.

Collection team about 850 including supervisors (about 700 front-end), up 150-200 in the period.

demand_pricing: Banks are moving to higher-ticket prime borrowers at single-digit pricing, leaving INR 10-25 lakh and INR 25+ lakh MSME segments with headroom for SBFC.

Gold competition rising as large players open branches; gold yields range 18-21%, with management expecting roughly 23% and possibly 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Gold price sensitivity and LTV risk.
qa_highlights.answer: LTV fell to 67% from about 70% last quarter (versus about 60s in June 2025). Auctions are triggered after 85-90% LTV and delinquency, with a 7-30 day window per management; out-of-money risk described as not significant.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of MSME disbursement pick-up.

qa_highlights.question: Collection headcount and bandwidth.

543960|2026-09.headline: Concord Biotech Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25% YoY to Rs 309.1 crore, but gross margin fell about 400 bps to 76.2%.
543960|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 25% YoY to Rs 309.1 crore and H1 grew 26% to Rs 566.6 crore, with API up 30% and formulations up 6%. Gross margin contracted about 400 bps to 76.2% on solvent and raw material cost increases, while reported EBITDA margin was 33.8% (33.0% for H1). Management attributed the weak formulation line to customers shifting to buying API and to business moving from Advergent to the US subsidiary Stellon. Injectables (Unit IV) and Stellon are still ramping, and management guided to contract wins in H2 and a 38-40% medium-term EBITDA margin.

+19% YoY; ex-JV share Rs 126.7 crore vs Rs 103.2 crore (+23%)

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 58.9 crore, +6% YoY; domestic formulations +29%. Weakness attributed to customers buying API instead of finished formulations in emerging markets and to business moving from Advergent to Stellon.

segments.name: Oncology
segments.commentary: Revenue nearly doubled YoY in H1 FY27, helped by Romidepsin and Everolimus.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: One commercial project; the opportunity under discussion is about $2 million annually, per management. Contract manufacturing for third parties is not classed as CDMO.

capex_capacity: Unit I utilisation 75%; Unit III (Limbasi) 55%; Unit II (oral solid, Valthera) 21%; Unit IV (Stellon injectables) 5%.

Fusidic acid being launched in emerging markets and then global markets; Fidaxomicin US DMF filed.
Management says there has been no pricing pressure; Concord has won share by offering significant price discounts to customers' existing suppliers.
Raw material cost increases (solvents) have not been passed on to customers; management says the rise is short-term and will be addressed through R&D and productivity.
Inspira dermatology division launched in the last couple of months; India dermatology market for the product range about Rs 5,000 crore; target of Rs 400-500 crore revenue in 4-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the API growth sustainable at a mid-teens rate, and what are the key products and drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said to build on the historical 18-19% API growth, with additional upside from injectables, CDMO and finished formulations. Growth is driven by anti-infectives, antifungals and oncology, with new customer additions.

543963|2026-03.headline: Shelter Pharma FY26 revenue rose 44% to INR 73.13 Cr with PAT of INR 9.03 Cr; management targets INR 200 Cr revenue by FY2030.
543963|2026-03.overview: Shelter Pharma reported FY26 revenue from operations of INR 73.13 Cr (up 44% YoY), EBITDA of INR 12.72 Cr (margin 17.39%, up 26% YoY) and PAT of INR 9.03 Cr (up 25% YoY). Q4 revenue was INR 39.84 Cr (up 50% YoY) and exports were about INR 6 Cr (up 164%). Management is expanding sales teams and distributors, which has compressed margins from roughly 20-21% in FY24-FY25, and working capital has stretched to 234 days with operating cash flow of minus INR 12.48 Cr. Management reiterated the INR 200 Cr FY2030 revenue target and outlined a second plant near Ahmedabad, with capex of about INR 12-15 Cr.

segments.name: Veterinary (animal health)
segments.commentary: About 55% of FY26 revenue. Leading products include Feedvet multivitamin powder, Lactocal calcium gel, Vymet D3+E liquid, Diarub bolus and Livodin liquid.

segments.name: Human healthcare
segments.commentary: About 45% of FY26 revenue. Key brands are Lemon & Barley Water (about INR 3.0-3.5 Cr revenue, no direct competition claimed), Sherolax, Gashoshel, Meryn, Joemega, All Vitamins and Omega-3 capsules. Management says human and veterinary margins are similar.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About INR 6 Cr in FY26, up 164%, mainly Africa and Middle East (UAE, Kuwait, Iraq, Qatar, Nepal, Bangladesh, Mauritius, Yemen, Sudan). Management says export margins are 20-25% higher than domestic; over INR 5 Cr already reached in Q1 FY27 per management.

Revenue mix goal of 40-45% human healthcare with similar margins.

Team: about 80 in sales, 12 in Ahmedabad office and 50 in the factory; sales team expected to double in two years.

demand_pricing: Management says the Ayurvedic market (INR 1,070 bn in 2025 to INR 3,728 bn by 2034, 15.52% CAGR) supports growth; organised players dominate value.

Africa, Middle East and state-government and central procurement (KPKB, CGHS, CSD) applications are being pursued; management says each African container is worth about INR 1-1.5 Cr.

Export order book size was not disclosed; management will follow up via Financial Minds.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said advances (about INR 37 Cr per an analyst's reading) are raw-material advances for long-term procurement and export pipeline orders; no return was specified.

qa_highlights.question: Why did promoter stake fall?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it was internal structuring: a family member was exiting part of the stake, and the promoter is buying stakes; not a promoter stake sale.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Middle East war hit margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pharma is treated as essential; three shipments are in transit to Africa and one to Dubai, with no margin impact expected.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 200 Cr target conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is realistic: exports were about INR 2.5 Cr in FY25 and about INR 6.5 Cr in FY26, with over INR 5 Cr already in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is planned for the next plant and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates INR 12-15 Cr, mostly from internal accruals, with installation starting around end-2027 after approvals from December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the EBITDA margin down from about 20% to 17%, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the dip to aggressive expansion in sales teams, channels and distributors; margins expected to stay similar this year or next, then rise to 22-25% in two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow negative and working capital at 234 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it moved from advance payments in three states to credit terms in new states; credit days were cut from 120 to 90 and are targeted at 60, then about one month.

qa_highlights.question: Why was preference equity of INR 42.44 Cr issued?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was mainly for working capital to fund a sales team that is expected to double in the next two years.

543965|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record Rs 3,032 crore (+21.3% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA rose 37.5% to Rs 222 crore, with a record Rs 524 crore of new business wins.
543965|2026-03.overview: TVS SCS posted its first Rs 3,000-plus crore revenue quarter, with ISCS growing 17.5% YoY and GFS 34.8% YoY on India ocean freight volumes. Adjusted EBITDA margin widened 80 bps YoY to 7.3%, driven by the Europe turnaround in ISCS and India volume growth in GFS. Full-year revenue grew 10.1% to Rs 11,003 crore and adjusted PBT rose 166% to Rs 99.3 crore. Management guided ISCS margin to 9.5-10% and group margin to about 7.3-7.4% for FY27, with GFS rates the key swing factor. The CEO-designate's first call also marked the retirement of MD Ravi Viswanathan.

segments.name: ISCS (Integrated Supply Chain Solutions)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 2,283 crore (+17.5% YoY); FY26 revenue Rs 8,238.9 crore (+9.6%). Adjusted EBITDA margin 9.3% in Q4, driven by Europe recovery and steady India growth; North America scaled up a large project live in H2 FY25.

segments.name: GFS (Global Forwarding Solutions)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 748.8 crore (+34.8% YoY) on India ocean freight volumes; FY26 revenue Rs 2,764.1 crore (+11.4%). Margin 2.4% in Q4 on volume growth and cost actions, but freight rates remain under pressure.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth expected in double digits, possibly early-to-mid teens, with ISCS a strong contributor.
ISCS adjusted EBITDA margin expected at 9.5-10% in FY27, versus 9.3% in Q4 FY26.
Group adjusted EBITDA margin expected around 7.3-7.4% in FY27, dependent on GFS freight rate trajectory.

Management expects PBT to grow sequentially every quarter; Swamy & Sons acquisition (completed in May 2026) expected to be margin accretive for India in FY27.
Depreciation and lease interest expected to change with a shift from long-term to short-term leases; ECL impairment expected slightly lower in FY27 than Rs 56 crore booked in FY26.

Credit rating India AA.

Fortune 500 active customers rose to 100 from 91, with 9 added in FY26.

Sectors with momentum include power (alternate energy), aerospace and defence (MOU with ALA), and China-plus-one relocations, which are still early.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for ISCS growth, potentially 18-20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pipeline supports it if conversion rises from about 22% to 23-25%. It set expectations at double-digit, early-to-mid-teens growth, and aspires to get closer to 18%.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margins should be expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: ISCS 9.5-10% from 9.3% in Q4; group about 7.3-7.4%, with GFS freight rates the main variable and management cautious on GFS.

qa_highlights.question: Why was part of the labour-code provision taken in Q4 rather than Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: A Labour Ministry clarification on 16 March came after Q3 results, requiring a reassessment and a Rs 5.2 crore additional provision in Q4. The company says the clarifications are now fully provided for.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impairment loss on financial instruments of about Rs 17.6 crore, and what is the FY27 trend?
qa_highlights.answer: It is an expected credit loss provision on customers, Rs 56 crore booked in FY26. Management expects the rate to be slightly lower in FY27, as most customers are highly rated B2B.

qa_highlights.question: Is the China-plus-one opportunity material?
qa_highlights.answer: Early traction with existing customers, including an earthmoving equipment company, but deals are not yet deep. Management is waiting to see whether US buyers accelerate expansion in India.

qa_highlights.question: What are the long-term targets for GFS and group revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not endorse a Rs 15,000 crore target by FY29-30; its long-term aspiration is early-teens EBITDA margins, with the GFS margin reaching 6-6.5%, the leader deferring to the incoming CEO.

543971|2026-03.headline: Bondada guides FY27 revenue growth of 60-70% on a INR7,147 crore order book; FY26 revenue reported at INR2,843 crore.
543971|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of about INR2,843 crore (vs INR1,571 crore in FY25) and a net profit of about INR211 crore, with the order book at INR7,147 crore as of 31 March 2026. Q4 EBITDA margin dipped on low-margin billing and higher steel and cable prices, which management says is not structural; FY26 margin rose about 30 bps to 7.5% from 7.2%. Cash from operations was positive at INR125 crore after collections above INR1,000 crore in Q4. New initiatives in BESS, data centres, defence and an IPP of 2 GW in Andhra Pradesh were highlighted as FY27 drivers.

segments.name: Renewable energy EPC
segments.commentary: Largest order book segment at INR4,536 crore (about 65% of total). About 1.3 GW commissioned cumulatively; about 0.5 GW commissioned in FY26 and target of about 1.5 GW in FY27, taking cumulative to about 3 GW.

segments.name: BESS
segments.commentary: Order book INR1,463 crore covering about 850 MW from Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh. Tamil Nadu 400 MWh due in about one year (financially closed, Canara Bank funding); AP 450 MWh due in about 18 months, financial closure pending.

segments.name: Telecom (BSNL)
segments.commentary: About 1,536 BSNL towers installed and about 1,506 on-air (about 99% strike rate). Management is pursuing Kavach railway passive-infrastructure tenders, with first win from South Central Railway.

segments.name: Services / O&M
segments.commentary: Management said O&M rose from about INR90 crore to about INR140 crore in FY26. An analyst's reading of a segment drop from about INR356 crore to INR140 crore was disputed; management said it would recheck the segmental reporting.

segments.name: Products and defence
segments.commentary: Products are targeted to rise from about 10% to 30% of mix (EPC 90% to 70%). First defence order is a missile component (BEL, about INR4 crore per analyst) with execution in about three months.

segments.name: Data centres
segments.commentary: One assignment under way in Hyderabad, with a second data centre in Vizag. Management expects 7-8% of FY27 revenue and EBITDA of 14-15%; no long-term capex planned.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 60-70% expected, with order book of about INR7,150 crore to be executed over 18-20 months.
Net profit growth of about 60-70% in absolute terms (analyst reading: 50-60% on bottom line); management said margins should be maintained.
EBITDA margin for FY27 to be flat or up 20-30 bps; Q1 margins expected to hold since materials were procured in advance.
Target 1.5 GW of solar EPC commissioning in FY27 and 7.8 GW portfolio to be commissioned over 2-2.5 years.
Vision 2030: 25 GW of renewable capacity (16 GW solar, 9 GW BESS) and about USD 1 billion revenue.
Migration to main board of BSE and NSE planned in FY27.
capex_capacity: Integrated manufacturing plant on about 27 acres near Hyderabad: capex INR120-130 crore including land; construction to start in Q2 FY27 with about one-year build time; incremental revenue expected from FY28.

AP 2 GW IPP via SPV, with about INR9,000 crore order value excluded from the INR7,147 crore order book; phased build of 250 MW first, then 500 MW tranches, full 2 GW by 2030, revenue from 2031; first 250 MW needs about INR250 crore equity.
GreenBond RE Park IPP targets 2 GW; IPP IRR expected about 17-18% for solar and 12-13% for BESS BOO projects.
Adani EPC order (about INR1,050 crore) at about 20% completion with plant to be commissioned by March 2027; management said it is slightly ahead of schedule.
demand_pricing: Tender participation of INR25,000-30,000 crore with a 20-25% win rate; about INR2,850 crore of L1 orders expected to convert in Q1 FY27.
Company stayed out of reverse auctions on some BESS tenders it considered unviable; it lost NTPC BESS tenders on price.
Receivable collections from NLC, NTPC, Singareni and MAHAGENCO with working capital of 85-90 days; PSU collection risk not seen.
Cable prices rose about 17-18% in the last quarter of FY26; steel also rose, with the increase seen as seasonal plus geopolitical. Some contracts are pass-through and some fixed.
Data-centre capex per MW of INR35-40 crore of company scope; starting size 2-3 MW, scalable to 10 MW.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 revenue and profit guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided about 60-70% revenue growth on the INR7,150 crore order book, with profit growing about 60-70% in absolute terms; an analyst's reading of 50-60% for the bottom line was not corrected.

qa_highlights.question: Q4 margin dip and whether FY27 margin of 11-12% EBITDA and 7% PAT is achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: The dip was attributed to low-margin billing in Q4 and higher steel and cable costs; the CMD said 11-12% EBITDA and about 7% PAT were achievable comfortably.

qa_highlights.question: Equity needs and funding for the 2 GW AP IPP?
qa_highlights.answer: Phased equity of about INR250 crore for the first 250 MW; the rest to be raised in tranches. Management said it has funding avenues and no immediate QIP plan was stated.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the company not part of recent NTPC and Coal India BESS tenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said recent BESS tenders were largely unviable; it bid in some NTPC tenders but was not L1, and stopped at reverse-auction thresholds.

qa_highlights.question: Data-centre margins and revenue share?
qa_highlights.answer: Data centres are expected to be 7-8% of FY27 revenue at EBITDA of 14-15%; the company will not hold long-term capex and aims to hand over shells and infrastructure.

qa_highlights.question: Segmental services revenue decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said O&M rose to about INR140 crore from INR90 crore and that some services had been reclassified into EPC; it said it would recheck the segment disclosure.

risks_watch: Segmental reporting inconsistency: services revenue figures in the quarterly disclosure were questioned and management committed to recheck.
Raw material inflation (steel, cables) and geopolitical effects on petroleum-linked inputs; Q1 FY27 margin guidance depends on procurement lock-in.
Working capital: current liabilities up sharply on TReDS and advances; receivables about 27-28% of revenue, aging 87 days, with some items over one year.
Execution risk: 1.5 GW commissioning target in FY27 and the Adani order commissioning by March 2027.
Funding and dilution for the 2 GW AP IPP and the AP BESS project financial closure, which was still pending.
Defence entry depends on trials of the missile component and on inorganic deals for three companies still in advanced talks.
Track L1 conversion of INR2,850 crore in Q1 FY27 and the Bryanston data-centre assignment.
543971|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on order book, growth and new segments, but defensive on the Q4 margin dip, segmental reporting questions and BESS pricing details, which were deferred to one-on-one meetings. Several answers were inconsistent or contradictory on figures (EBITDA, revenue guidance), which lowers confidence in the precision of guidance.
key_quotes: So having said this, maybe anything around 60% to 70% of revenue growth will be there even coming financial year.
We're making it ready and then giving back to the hyperscalers. So we are not going to sit on any Capex in long term.
EBITDA margins for this year will remain same or maybe we will have a little improved margins of by about 20, 30 basis points yes.

rows.why: Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin flat to up 20-30 bps from FY26 ~7.5%, with Q1 margins expected to hold because materials were procured in advance; cable prices rose ~17-18% and steel rose in Q4 FY26, and some contracts are fixed-price, so the expansion is not assured.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.why: About 0.5 GW commissioned in FY26 and a 1.5 GW FY27 target takes cumulative capacity from ~1.3 GW to ~3 GW; Adani EPC (~INR1,050 cr) is ~20% complete and slightly ahead of schedule.

rows.why: Revenue growth guided at 60-70% on a INR7,147 cr order book to be executed over 18-20 months; FY26 revenue rose ~81% to INR2,843 cr from INR1,571 cr.

rows.why: Integrated manufacturing plant on ~27 acres near Hyderabad (INR120-130 cr incl. land) is already planned with construction in Q2 FY27, and 2 GW AP IPP needs ~INR250 cr first-phase equity, so further capex is guided rather than just hinted.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 60-70% and ~INR2,850 cr of L1 orders expected to convert in Q1 FY27, but Q4 margin dip and the analyst's 50-60% profit reading show guidance is not yet clearly ahead of plan.

rows.why: Q4 margin dip from low-margin billing and steel/cable inflation, Q1 margin hold depends on procurement lock-in, and the 1.5 GW commissioning and Adani plant by March 2027 are execution-heavy; management guidance figures were also inconsistent on the call.

rows.why: Products targeted to rise from ~10% to ~30% of mix; first defence order is a missile component (BEL, ~INR4 cr per analyst) with execution in ~3 months, and data centres are 7-8% of FY27 revenue at 14-15% EBITDA with Hyderabad under way and Vizag next.

rows.why: Order book of INR7,147 cr (RE INR4,536 cr, BESS INR1,463 cr) with about INR2,850 cr of L1 orders expected to convert in Q1 FY27 out of INR25,000-30,000 cr tenders at a 20-25% win rate.

rows.why: Receivables ~27-28% of revenue (INR760-791 cr), average aging 87 days, with some items over one year; Q4 collections exceeded INR1,000 cr and FY26 operating cash flow turned positive at INR125 cr.

rows.label: AP 2 GW IPP and BESS financial closures
rows.why: AP 2 GW IPP (~INR9,000 cr order value, excluded from order book) starts with 250 MW needing ~INR250 cr equity; AP 450 MWh BESS financial closure pending, so funding conditions decide timing.

543972|2026-03.headline: Aeroflex Q4 FY26 total income rose 38% YoY to INR126.5 crore with EBITDA margin of 23.86%; skid assemblies scaling to 15,000 units per annum.
543972|2026-03.overview: Management reported record Q4 and FY26 performance, with Q4 total income of INR126.5 crore (+38% YoY), EBITDA of INR30 crore (+59%) and PAT of INR17.6 crore (+57%). FY26 total income was INR443.3 crore (+17%), EBITDA INR99.7 crore (+26%) and PAT INR55.5 crore. The new liquid cooling skid assemblies business contributed about 5% of FY26 sales, with 617 skids sold, and capacity is being lifted from 6,000 to 15,000 units per annum within about two quarters. Management flagged design and customer quality-audit bottlenecks that delayed skid supply, and guided FY27 growth of about 35% with base business growth of 15-20%.

financial_highlights.change: Majority of sales in Q3 and Q4

segments.name: Liquid cooling skid assemblies
segments.commentary: 617 skids sold in FY26 for ~INR21.2 crore, all in India and supplied to one exclusive principal; ~5% of FY26 sales, guided to 20-22% of FY27 sales. Average selling price guided at INR3-3.25 lakh per skid.

segments.name: Hoses and assemblies (value-added)
segments.commentary: Value-added products (assemblies, fittings and bellows) were 52% of FY26 sales. Management said hose assemblies remain the core business for the next 2-3 years, with 75-80% of hose assembly sales from exports.

segments.name: Metal bellows
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR8 crore, utilisation below 20%; peak revenue potential about INR80 crore at ~85% utilisation. Targeting 50-60% utilisation in 2-3 years. Management called it the highest-margin product.

segments.name: Hyd-Air (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR31.64 crore; utilisation about 60%. Capacity to be used mainly for in-house fittings and connectors for Aeroflex's own projects.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Domestic share rose to 31% of FY26 sales from 26%, with domestic sales up about 40% in Q4. Exports still about 60%; exports grew in double digits in Q4 per management. Largest international customer is 25-26% of sales.

guidance_outlook: FY27 total growth guided at about 35%, with base business growth of 15-20%.
FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin target around 23% (FY26 was 22.6%); around 25% over the next couple of years.
Skid assembly capacity to rise from 6,000 to 15,000 units per annum within about two quarters.
Skid utilisation target of 60-70% by March 2027 (March closing month, not full-year average); peak utilisation 75-80%.
At 75% utilisation, 15,000-skid capacity implies revenue of about INR325-330 crore for the skid business.
Some skid supply to international markets targeted within FY27; no finalised plan yet.
Expected sales from new data centre hose products (last-mile cooling, firefighting) from next quarter; annealing furnace due by end of 2026.
capex_capacity: Skid assemblies capacity scaled from 2,000 to 6,000 units per annum; expansion to 15,000 per annum targeted within about two quarters; management said further expansion beyond 15,000 is the ultimate aim but not the current focus.
Two robotic welding lines commissioned to improve automation and precision.
New annealing furnace targeted for commissioning by end of calendar 2026.
Miniature metal bellows capacity at 60,000 pieces; no further expansion planned this year, with capital redeployed to liquid cooling.
Hyd-Air utilisation about 60%, with plans to absorb in-house demand rather than add capex.
demand_pricing: Management said the liquid cooling TAM is about INR3 billion growing to about INR21 billion in 5-6 years (~34-35% CAGR), and liquid cooling is about 10-11% of data centre cost.
Skid supply is currently behind demand, with the principal's design work now done in-house and end-customer quality audits adding time; management expects smoothing over the next couple of months.
Orders for skids are visible only from the one exclusive principal; other customer talks have just begun.
Management said Aeroflex is among the only Indian skid manufacturers and competes more on supply than price; overseas landed-cost pricing for hoses is about 25-30% cheaper than local alternatives.
US tariffs: Section 232 tariff on products reduced from around mid-February; current rate cited as 10-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Order book for liquid cooling skids and planned utilisation for 15,000 capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book not disclosed due to agreement; a full-year pipeline is shared by the principal and broken into quarterly POs. Peak utilisation 75-80%; target 60-70% by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why did skid execution lag last quarter's expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Bottlenecks are design finalisation (earlier done by principal, now in-house) and rigorous end-customer quality and welding audits, which management expects to ease over a couple of months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the export share decline (from ~69% to ~60%) the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exports rose in double digits in Q4; the ratio shifted because domestic sales grew about 40%. Skid sales will be domestic, so the domestic share will rise further.

qa_highlights.question: Metal bellows FY26 revenue, utilisation and path to scale?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 revenue about INR8 crore, utilisation below 20%, ARR about INR12 crore; targeting 50-60% utilisation in 2-3 years, with sales cycles longer than other products.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR40 crore income tax demand (AY 2018-19) a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand relates to a reopened assessment on a bank interest waiver from the company's takeover of a stressed entity. Management said disclosures were made and advisers are confident of reversal on appeal; no timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin and ASP outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Skid margin is in line with company average (not disclosed separately). ASP guided INR3-3.25 lakh per skid versus about INR3.4 lakh cited by an analyst for FY26.

risks_watch: Skid execution depends on design sign-off and end-customer quality audits; delays could push revenue below the 15,000-unit ramp.
Concentration risk: skid business rests on one exclusive principal, and order book is not disclosed.
INR40 crore income tax demand (AY 2018-19) is roughly equal to FY26 PAT and is under appeal with no timeline.
Metal bellows utilisation below 20% with long sales cycles; the 50-60% target is 2-3 years out.
Tariff and geopolitical exposure: about 60% of sales are exports, and management cited West Asia developments and US tariff swings during FY26.
Watch Q1 FY27 for skid revenue ramp, the first international skid supply and the annealing furnace commissioning.
